- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

<function call omitted for brevity>

assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

</commentary>

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. - pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Critical finding baked into that doc: **no SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook/price data** — price sync must always go through file-based WebDAV import regardless of pattern chosen. That doc's own Open Items (rate limits, bulk-operation support, Anypoint MQ sequencing) are still unanswered. "Mulesoft API Spec - Hub" (305659907) is a completely empty stub. Dependencies tracker row T2 "SFCC MRT API Capabilities" has blank SME Owner/Status.

"Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (318472193) covers environment topology, alias/release workflow, token scoping, and locale config (9 locale codes across 8 storefronts) — largely answers the spike's environment/locale tasks. "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208) §6 already states the handoff boundary: Contentful owns only editorial content (banners/collection pages/lookbook/rich PDP copy) via Delivery API; all product/price/inventory data stays in SFCC via AP21→MuleSoft, never Contentful. That same TSD's Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope | Frontend Dev | Open") is effectively the same deliverable as SFCC-123 — worth cross-linking. Still genuinely open: Sprint 1/2 required content types beyond the current `shoppableImage`/`CollectionHero`/`ImageText` set, and which specific Contentful fields/rendering logic SFCC needs to consume. Several Human Setup Checklist items on the ops page are incomplete (MRT env vars per tier not set, cache-purge webhook not configured, content-type-editing roles not restricted, CI CMA token not added as a GH secret) — worth flagging as blockers per the spike's own task list.

This conflicts with AGENTS.md/testing.md's "11 active locales" figure for the same 8 storefronts — a real inconsistency that should be resolved as part of SFCC-123's locale task, since it affects Contentful locale bootstrap scope. Not yet raised with the user.
17	
18	**Why:** these two spikes were the user's active assigned work as of 2026-07-15; both link to the Dependencies tracker (310050860) rows T1/T2, which are Sprint 1 blockers for Squad A.
19	**How to apply:** when picking this work back up, start from the specific pages named above rather than re-searching from scratch — they cover most of each spike's DoD already. Flag the locale-count discrepancy to the user before it gets baked into a finalized TSD.

Audited the SFCC Confluence space for existing documentation/support for two assigned spikes. Full page inventory in [[reference-confluence-sfcc-space]]. Key findings:

**SFCC-122 (MRT API Capabilities):** No single canonical doc exists — the spike is genuinely needed, not duplicative. Closest existing material is "TSD: Catalogue Sync — SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)" (315490342), which documents SCAPI Admin APIs for Product/Inventory as an alternative to the recommended WebDAV file-based import. Critical finding baked into that doc: **no SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook/price data** — price sync must always go through file-based WebDAV import regardless of pattern chosen. That doc's own Open Items (rate limits, bulk-operation support, Anypoint MQ sequencing) are still unanswered. "Mulesoft API Spec - Hub" (305659907) is a completely empty stub. Dependencies tracker row T2 "SFCC MRT API Capabilities" has blank SME Owner/Status.

**SFCC-123 (Contentful Integration TSD):** Strong head start already exists. "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (318472193) covers environment topology, alias/release workflow, token scoping, and locale config (9 locale codes across 8 storefronts) — largely answers the spike's environment/locale tasks. "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" (292061208) §6 already states the handoff boundary: Contentful owns only editorial content (banners/collection pages/lookbook/rich PDP copy) via Delivery API; all product/price/inventory data stays in SFCC via AP21→MuleSoft, never Contentful. That same TSD's Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope | Frontend Dev | Open") is effectively the same deliverable as SFCC-123 — worth cross-linking. Still genuinely open: Sprint 1/2 required content types beyond the current `shoppableImage`/`CollectionHero`/`ImageText` set, and which specific Contentful fields/rendering logic SFCC needs to consume. Several Human Setup Checklist items on the ops page are incomplete (MRT env vars per tier not set, cache-purge webhook not configured, content-type-editing roles not restricted, CI CMA token not added as a GH secret) — worth flagging as blockers per the spike's own task list.

**Discrepancy found:** Both Confluence locale tables (Contentful ops page and the Product TSD's multi-locale table) agree on 9 unique locale codes for the 8 storefronts (en, en-GB, en-US, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE). This conflicts with AGENTS.md/testing.md's "11 active locales" figure for the same 8 storefronts — a real inconsistency that should be resolved as part of SFCC-123's locale task, since it affects Contentful locale bootstrap scope. Not yet raised with the user.

**Why:** these two spikes were the user's active assigned work as of 2026-07-15; both link to the Dependencies tracker (310050860) rows T1/T2, which are Sprint 1 blockers for Squad A.
**How to apply:** when picking this work back up, start from the specific pages named above rather than re-searching from scratch — they cover most of each spike's DoD already. Flag the locale-count discrepancy to the user before it gets baked into a finalized TSD.

Once both complete, I'll synthesize everything into a structured guardrails document.

The goal is to produce a thorough, structured inventory of every software-engineering "harness" or "guardrail" mechanism in this codebase — i.e. anything that automatically enforces quality, security, or process rules (as opposed to rules that rely purely on a human/Claude reading a doc).

I (the calling session) already have full contents of these files in context, so do NOT re-summarize them for me — just reference them by path if relevant: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/conventions.md, .claude/rules/css.md, .claude/rules/components.md, .claude/rules/typescript.md, .claude/rules/testing.md, .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md, .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md.

Please investigate and report back on each of the following, with concrete details (exact file paths, key config values, job/check names, thresholds, secrets referenced by name only not value):

1. **CI/CD pipeline** — read all files under `.github/workflows/`. For each workflow: trigger conditions, jobs, what it gates (required status check?), and anything enforcing Tier 1/2 file protection (e.g. protected-file-guard.yml), branch-specific behavior (release/** vs develop-targeted PRs), the change-scoped E2E logic in qa.yml, BrowserStack story-scoping logic, and any Lighthouse/perf budget gate (lighthouserc.js is Tier1 — check if referenced in a workflow).
2. **CODEOWNERS** — read the file, report exactly which paths route to which teams.
3. **AI PR review tooling** — read `coderabbit.yaml` and enumerate rules under `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` (list rule names/what each checks — accessibility, hardcoded values, etc.), and `semgrep.yml` (list rule ids/what each detects, especially payment-credential-logging and XSS/dangerouslySetInnerHTML rules).
4. **Git hooks** — read `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` and `scripts/hooks/commit-msg` in full. Report exactly what each enforces (conventional commits format, Contentful drift check, secret-guard for .env.sample, blocking direct edits to derived AI config files, etc.) and how they're wired up (husky? core.hooksPath? check package.json "prepare" script or similar).
5. **TypeScript/lint/build enforcement** — read tsconfig.json (strict mode flags), .eslintrc.js or eslint config (rules configured, especially anything about complexity/max-lines-per-function — confirm AGENTS.md's claim that these are NOT configured), babel.config.js (path aliases), and package.json scripts (build, lint, tsc, test, push, env).
6. **Test harness config** — vitest.config.*, vitest.setup.ts, playwright.config.*, .storybook/ config, .browserstack.yml — report key settings (coverage thresholds if any, test environment setup, projects configured).
7. **Environment & secrets tooling** — scripts/switchEnv.mjs (what npm run env subcommands exist, the scope:shared|tier|personal|auto tagging, the push-to-GitHub-Environments gate), .env.sample header (full command reference), and how secrets are prevented from leaking (pre-commit secret guard details from step 4).
8. **Contentful sync safety** — scripts/contentful/sync.js and scripts/contentful/content-types/ — confirm the additive-only idempotent behavior claim and any safety checks in the script itself.
9. **Dependency/package protections** — check if there's a Renovate/Dependabot config, and confirm package.json root is Tier 1 per frozenFiles.md.
10. **Docs that encode process guardrails** — read .docs/releaseBranchesRules.md, .docs/architecture.md (just the guardrail-relevant parts: path aliases, overrides pattern boundaries), .docs/upstreamPolicy.md if it exists, and list what's under .docs/memory/ (just filenames + one-line purpose, don't dump contents).
11. **.claude/settings.json** — read it and report any permission rules, hooks, or other harness config configured there.
12. Any other automated guardrail you find that doesn't fit above (e.g. a GitHub branch protection reference in docs, a required-reviewers config, ast-grep or semgrep configs elsewhere).

Report back in a structured format organized by the 12 numbered categories above, with file paths cited for everything. Be thorough but concise — bullet points with concrete facts, not prose. This report will be used to write a comprehensive guardrails document, so completeness and accuracy matter more than brevity, but avoid including full file contents verbatim — extract and summarize the enforcement logic instead.

<result># Confluence Guardrails Audit — SFCC Space

All pages fetched successfully (read-only; no edits made). Findings below, organized per the 8 requested categories plus a 9th for additional discoveries from the search step.

---

## 1. Branching Guide (GitFlow) — page 304840733

**Approval counts per branch:**
- `feature/*` → `develop`: **1 approval** required ("develop is a shared integration point")
- `fix/*` → `develop`: same as feature (1 approval, via `qa.yml` unit tests)
- `hotfix/*` → `main` **and** `develop`: approvals not stated on this page (see CI/CD page: 2)
- `release/**`: created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state — developers do not create these directly
- `fix/release-{version}-*` → `release/**`: PR back into the release branch; squad leads separately apply the same fix to `develop` via a second PR
- Direct commits to a release branch: only for **no-logic changes** (copy corrections, version bumps, boolean flag toggles) — require **explicit squad lead approval**

**Release tagging process:** `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` after the release PR merges — creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` git tags. Sprint boundary tags (`sprint/{N}/{date}`) are created automatically by CI when `scripts/sprint.txt` is updated.

**Version format:** Pre-go-live `v0.{sprint}.0`; go-live `v1.0.0`; post-launch patches `v1.0.{patch}`; post-launch features `v1.{minor}.0`.

**Merge restrictions:** Claude Code is "physically blocked" from writing to `develop`/`main` via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. On `release/**`, Claude Code runs in supervised/read-only-skills mode; code logic fixes must go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch.

---

## 2. PWA CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions) — page 305561601

**Trigger matrix (workflow → jobs):**
- Push to `develop` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate → deploy-sit → tag-sit-deploy, tag-sprint
- PR → `release/**` → `digital-sit.yml`: install → four signal jobs → sit-gate (no deploy)
- PR → `develop` or `release/**` → `qa.yml`: unit-tests, storybook-test (every PR) → e2e-browserstack (release/** only)
- PR opened (any branch) → `protected-file-guard.yml`: tier-1-guard, tier-2-guard
- Weekly cron (Mon 1am UTC) → `weekly-agents.yml`: quality-sweep, contentful-drift-audit, changelog-reminder
- Weekly cron (Mon 0:00 UTC) → `upstream-release-watch.yml`: check-for-new-release

**Branch protection — required approvals:**
- `develop`: **2 approvals** (one owning squad, one cross-squad), required status check `unit-tests`, branches must be up to date, no bypass
- `main`: **2 approvals** (both squad leads), same up-to-date/no-bypass rules; hotfix PRs into `main` still require 2 approvals
- `release/**`: required check = `Digital SIT Gate` composite job

**Digital SIT Gate thresholds (also gates `release/**` merges):**
| Signal | Tool | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright P0 | Playwright | 100% pass, all storefront configs |
| Lighthouse CI | LHCI | Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop = blocked |
| MuleSoft contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI | Any schema breach = blocked (pending spec source) |
| Bundle size | bundlewatch | main.js <180kB, vendor.js <250kB, main.css <50kB |

**STAGE convergence gate:** manual, not a GitHub status check — checklist: Digital SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead and both squad leads signed off.

**Commit message enforcement:** Layer 1 = local `commit-msg` Husky hook (types: feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/perf/test/build/ci/chore/upstream-sync). Layer 2 = CodeRabbit PR review (`coderabbit.yaml`).

**CI Secrets (names only):** `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT`, `MRT_USER`, `MRT_API_KEY`, `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT`, `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`.

---

## 3. SIT Quality Gates — page 304840754

- Four automated checks gate promotion to `release/**` — enforced by GitHub branch protection; cannot merge without green `Digital SIT Gate`.
- **Thresholds** (same as above): Playwright P0 100% pass; Lighthouse Perf ≥80/A11y ≥90/Best Practices ≥90 (>5pt drop blocks); bundle main.js<180kB/vendor.js<250kB/main.css<50kB; contract tests = any breach blocks.
- Playwright `retries` intentionally set to **0** — flaky tests must be fixed, not retried away.
- **Open dependency:** `test:contracts` currently exits 0 with a warning — not a real assertion yet (owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead).
- **Secrets:** `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` (Lighthouse); `BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`, `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT`, all `E2E_*` SKU secrets (BrowserStack, `qa.yml` on `release/**` PRs only, Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge).

---

## 4. AI-Assisted QA Six-Stage Pipeline — pages 277544962 (parent), 277577757, 277708807, 277676053, 305528833

| Stage | Gate/check represented |
|---|---|
| 1 — Story Intake | BA structures Jira story to a fixed template (role, goal, in/out of scope, regions, edge cases) — no gate yet, but poor input here degrades every downstream stage |
| 2 — AC Authoring with Claude | **HUMAN GATE 1**: BA must review every AC line and set Jira status to "AC Approved" before Zephyr work begins |
| 3 — Zephyr Test Case Creation via MCP | **HUMAN GATE 2**: Tester reviews steps/expected results and marks each case "Ready for Execution"; nothing is created in Zephyr before review |

**`.storybook/main.js`**: stories glob `../overrides/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx|mdx)`, addons include `@storybook/addon-a11y`; `webpackFinal` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app`/`pwa-kit-react-sdk`/`pwa-kit-runtime`/`commerce-sdk-react` to `node_modules`, plus the project `~`/`app` aliases. **`.storybook/preview.tsx`**: `a11y.test: 'error'` — a11y violations **fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs; excludes Chakra's toast-manager regions from a11y checks (known upstream limitation).

**`.browserstack.yml`**: `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope enforcement per frozenFiles.md's "scope change = CI cost explosion" note); browsers: Chrome (macOS Sonoma), Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox (Windows 11), Edge (Windows 11); `testObservability: true` linking to Zephyr via `buildName: Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}`; `parallelsPerPlatform: 2`.

**`lighthouserc.js`**: `numberOfRuns: 3`; assertions — `categories:performance` ≥0.80 (error), `categories:accessibility` ≥0.90 (error), `categories:best-practices` ≥0.90 (error), preset `lighthouse:recommended`; upload target is `lhci` server if `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL` set, else `temporary-public-storage`.

### 7. Environment & secrets tooling

**`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** subcommands: (none) → report current tier; `init` → scaffolds `.env.shared` + all six `.env.<tier>` files, pulls values from GitHub Environments (`gh variable list --env <scope>`), auto-fetches Contentful tokens; `validate [--live]` → cross-checks key placement (shared vs tier vs personal vs auto), flags typos/misplaced keys, and with `--live` makes a real read-only Contentful Delivery API call + a real SLAS guest-token request per tier; `push <shared|dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod>` → **gated to tier-1-approvers only** via `isTier1Approver()` (`gh api user --jq .login` + `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members`), excludes `scope:personal` keys from ever being pushed/pulled centrally; `<tier>` → merges `.env.shared` + `.env.<tier>` into `.env` (tier wins), stamps `ENVIRONMENT_NAME`/`DEPLOY_TARGET`.

**`.env.sample`** header documents the full command reference (matches above) plus the `scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` tagging convention — scope tag must be its own comment line above `KEY=value` (not trailing), specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard. Documents a deliberate, confirmed override: GitHub Environment Variables are plaintext/readable by any repo collaborator, a conscious tradeoff accepted for centralization (write gated to repo Admin = tier-1-approvers).

**Secret-leak prevention**: the pre-commit hook's `.env.sample` guard (section 4 above) is the main mechanical control; `gitleaks` (via `coderabbit.yaml` tools) is a second, PR-time layer.

### 8. Contentful sync safety

**`scripts/contentful/sync.js`**: reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`/`CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`/`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, iterates `.js` files in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` (currently just `shoppableImage.js`), calls `upsertContentType()` per file. **Additive-only confirmed in code**: on update, `ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]` — explicitly preserves existing fields not present in the local definition, never deletes a field from a live content type; each type is published after upsert. `.docs/architecture.md` and `AGENTS.md` both state this idempotent/additive behavior, and the code matches.

### 9. Dependency/package protections

**No Renovate or Dependabot config found anywhere in the repo** (`find` for `renovate*`/`dependabot*` returned nothing outside `node_modules`) — dependency updates are entirely manual/PR-based, with `coderabbit.yaml`'s `auto_review.ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]` implying dependency-bump PRs were anticipated but no bot is actually configured to open them. Root `package.json` is confirmed Tier 1 in `frozenFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` (`package.json → @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), and `protected-file-guard.yml`'s tier1 file list — consistent across all three enforcement surfaces. `osvScanner` (CodeRabbit tool) provides dependency-vulnerability scanning as a partial substitute for a dependency-bump bot.

### 10. Docs encoding process guardrails

- **`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`**: back-merge rules (release→main triggers back-merge to develop; hotfix→main same), and the release-branch supervised-edit protocol (state plan → assess blast radius/consumer count → wait for explicit confirmation before any edit) plus the `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch requirement for code logic fixes.
- **`.docs/architecture.md`** (guardrail-relevant parts): confirms path-alias sync group is actually **5** files, not 4 (`babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `jest.config.js` moduleNameMapper, `vitest.config.ts`) — `jest.config.js` is called out as a separate group for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only, not part of the 4-way sync AGENTS.md describes. Documents the overrides-pattern copy-first flow (copy → convert → `tsc --noEmit` → stop for approval) and SSR mandate (DMU-030 — SSR must be preserved for product/category/content pages, no client-only shortcuts). Also documents `undici` per-origin connection-pool isolation in `overrides/app/ssr.js`/`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` as blast-radius mitigation.
- **`.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`**: "bump opportunistically, not on a schedule" policy tied to `upstream-release-watch.yml`; explicitly states there is **no drift-detection script** (drift is the point of the overrides pattern) and **no two-track review**.
- **`.docs/memory/`** contents: `projectState.md` (current status of all services/integrations/deploy state, updated each session), `feedback.md` (what worked/failed/gotchas learned), `references.md` (service URLs/credentials/dashboard locations), `sprintScope.md` (draft dependency order of the build — gates what Claude may assume exists), `upstreamBaseline.md` (pinned `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version + `<!-- upstream-release-tag -->` marker consumed by the watch workflow).

### 11. `.claude/settings.json`

- **`PreToolUse`** hook on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: (a) blocks any file write if `git branch --show-current` is `develop` or `main` (`exit 1` with a BLOCKED message) — this is the actual mechanical enforcement of Hard Rule #1/#3 in the branch table, not just documentation; (b) runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present.
- **`PostToolUse`** hooks: on `Write` — auto-runs Prettier on the new file; on `Edit|Write` — runs `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (referenced but not found on disk — dangling reference) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh`; on `Write` — runs `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh`.
- **`Stop`** hook: runs `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh`.
- **`permissions.allow`**: pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash patterns (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so Claude isn't prompted for these every time.
- **`.claude/settings.local.json`** (session-specific, not checked in for team-wide enforcement): allows specific MCP/Bash patterns (`gh api user`, `mcp-atlassian`, `git checkout/fetch`, a specific `WebFetch` domain), `enableAllProjectMcpServers: true`, enables `mcp-atlassian`.

Client-side hook scripts (all in `.claude/hooks/`, all **non-blocking**, `exit 0` always):
- `tier2Warn.sh` — regex-matches the edited file path against Tier 2 groups (global shell, shared product/commerce components, theme component styles, shared hooks, translations) and prints an owner/notify warning.
- `registryUpdate.sh` — incrementally regenerates `.claude/registry/` entries for the specific edited file (components/hooks/utils/pages/routes), skipping test/story/ContentfulDefinition files.
- `testFileRemind.sh` — after writing a new component/hook source file, checks for a co-located `.test.*` file and prints a reminder (not a block) if missing.
- `session-reflect.sh` — Stop hook that, if anything changed this session, returns `{decision: "block", reason: ...}` forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/<timestamp>-<branch>.md` suggesting doc updates (AGENTS.md, architecture.md, memory files, rule tiers) — explicitly forbidden from editing those docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard (`stop_hook_active`) to avoid infinite loop.

### 12. Other guardrails found

- **`.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`** — squad territory maps with YAML frontmatter `paths:` lists, consumed by the `scope-check` skill and referenced by `.claude/skills/audit-tier` for Tier 3 classification; not enforced mechanically (draft status noted — "squad split can still change").
- **`.claude/skills/scope-check/SKILL.md`** — a pre-flight tool: classifies every file a proposed prompt would likely touch by tier (1–4), verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, and rewrites unsafe prompts — a guardrail applied *before* Claude acts, not after.
- **`scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`** — the generator behind the pre-commit hook's derived-file sync; supports `--check` (CI-style drift detection, exit 1 on drift) and `--fix` modes; keeps `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.vscode/instructions/*.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` in sync with `.claude/rules/*.md` + `AGENTS.md` so multiple AI tools see consistent rules.
- **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`** — structured checklist enforcing (via human/reviewer discipline, not CI): squad ownership ticking, breaking-change definition, protection-tier self-check (referencing `/audit-tier`), `npx tsc --noEmit`/lint/test/storybook checklist, WCAG 2.1 AA minimum bar, localisation (18 locale files), third-party-integration degradation notes.
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`** — `bug_report.md`, `feature_request.md` (not deeply inspected, standard issue templates).
- **No dedicated ast-grep or semgrep config exists outside `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` and root `semgrep.yml`** — both are Tier 1 per `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS/`protected-file-guard.yml` consistently.
- **Discrepancy worth flagging**: `package.json`'s `test:lighthouse` script points at `tests/lighthouserc.js`, and `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS both list `tests/lighthouserc.js` as a Tier 1 path — but no `tests/` directory exists in the repo; only the root `lighthouserc.js` is real and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually executes via `lhci autorun` (implicit default config resolution, no `--config` flag passed in the workflow). This is a latent doc/script drift, not a currently-broken gate, since the workflow doesn't reference the missing path directly.</result>

input.content: # Zimmermann PWA Kit — Software Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails _Compiled from a full sweep of the `zimmermann-pwa` repo and the Confluence `SFCC` space, 2026-07-16._ _Scope: mechanisms that automatically enforce quality, security, or process — not general conventions that rely on a human/Claude reading a doc._ --- ## 1. Branch & Merge Guardrails | Branch | From | Merges to | Required approvals | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | `feature/*`, `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | **1** (unit-tests required check) | Primary working branches | | `release/**` | `develop` | `main` + `develop` | Required check = **Digital SIT Gate** (composite) | Created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state, not by developers directly | | `fix/release-{version}-*` | `release/**` | `release/**`, then forward-merged to `develop` | Treated like `feature/*` | Only path for code-logic fixes on a release | | `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` + `develop` | **2** (both squad leads) | Urgent prod fixes only, must back-merge to `develop` | | `develop` | — | — | **2** (one owning squad + one cross-squad) | Human commits only; required check `unit-tests`, no bypass, must be up to date | | `main` | — | — | **2** (both squad leads) | Human commits only; same no-bypass rules | - **Mechanical branch lock (not just documented):** `.claude/settings.json` has a `PreToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit` that runs `git branch --show-current` and hard-blocks (`exit 1`) any file write if the branch is `develop` or `main`. This is the actual enforcement of AGENTS.md Hard Rule #1 for Claude Code sessions — GitHub branch protection is the enforcement for everyone/everything else. - **`branch-target-guard`** (`protected-file-guard.yml`) hard-blocks (`exit 1`) a PR from a `feature/*` head branch targeting `main` directly. - Release tagging: `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` post-merge creates `v{version}` + `release/digital/v{version}` tags; `sprint/{N}/{date}` tags are created automatically by CI (`deploy-dev.yml`'s `tag-sprint` job) when `scripts/sprint.txt` changes. - Direct commits to a `release/**` branch are restricted to no-logic changes (copy fixes, version bumps, flag toggles) and require explicit squad-lead approval (Confluence: Branching Guide, page 304840733). --- ## 2. File Protection Tiers Four-tier system, cross-checked across `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, and `protected-file-guard.yml` — all three enforcement surfaces agree. | Tier | Examples | Enforcement | |---|---|---| | **Tier 1 — Frozen** | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`, Tier-1 commerce hooks (`use-current-basket.ts`, `use-current-customer.ts`, `use-navigation.ts`, `use-multi-site.ts`, `use-einstein.ts`, `use-datacloud.ts`, `use-refresh-token.ts`), `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js` + `ssr/`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, `mobify.config.js`, `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, test/tooling configs (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js`, `.browserstack.yml`), `.github/workflows/`, governance files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.claude/rules/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/`, `semgrep.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`) | CODEOWNERS routes to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`; branch protection requires a code-owner approving review before merge (the real, working gate); `tier1-guard` job posts a non-blocking warning + owner map (can't be a hard-fail required check — GitHub disabled cross-run check-run status updates in Feb 2025) | | **Tier 2 — Protected** | Global shell (`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`, `routes.tsx`), shared product components (`product-tile/`, `product-item/`, `display-price/`, `image-gallery/`, `swatch-group/`, `recommended-products/`), shared commerce components (`order-summary/`, `promo-code/`, `pickup-or-delivery/`), `theme/components/`, `translations/`, 8 named shared hooks (5+ consumers), `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/sync.js` + `content-types/` | CODEOWNERS routes to owning squad team **+** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers` **+** `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (Tier-1 approvers can also clear Tier 2); `tier2-warning` job posts a non-blocking PR comment listing changed files + reviewer checklist | | **Tier 3 — Squad territory** | e.g. `overrides/app/pages/cart/` → Squad A, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → Squad B | CODEOWNERS routes to the owning squad only, no approver gate; `cross-squad-guard` posts a non-blocking comment if a single PR touches both squads' territory | | **Unclassified** | Everything else under `overrides/` | Normal feature-branch workflow | - Required-status-check strings referenced in the Confluence CI/CD setup checklist (305430530): `🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning`, `🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check` — the 🔴 items are hard-fail/required, the 🟡 items are warning-only. - GitHub teams backing CODEOWNERS: `design-system`, `integration-lead`, `squad-a-lead`, `squad-b-lead`, `squad-leads`, `pwa-squad-a`, `pwa-squad-b`, `tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, `pwa-qa-team` (owns `e2e/`). --- ## 3. CI/CD Pipeline (`.github/workflows/`) | Workflow | Trigger | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `qa.yml` | PR → `develop` or `release/**` | Required check. `detect-changes` computes scoped booleans (`storybook`/`e2e`/`vitest`) from changed files since the previous push (not merge-base) via job-level `if:` rather than `on.paths`, so a skipped job still reports "success" instead of leaving the check stuck pending. Jobs: `unit-tests` (Vitest), `storybook-test` (`@storybook/test-runner` + `addon-a11y`), `e2e-localhost` (Playwright chromium + mobile-chrome, 15 min timeout), `e2e-browserstack` (develop-targeted PRs only run if a `SFCC-\d+` Jira key is found in title/body/branch; `release/**` PRs always run the full suite unscoped) | | `protected-file-guard.yml` | PR → `develop`/`main`/`release/**` | `tier1-guard` (warning), `branch-target-guard` (hard block), `tier2-warning` (warning), `cross-squad-guard` (warning) — see §2 | | `digital-sit.yml` ("SIT Gate") | Push/PR → `release/**` | `playwright-p0`, `lighthouse-ci` (`lhci autorun`), `contract-tests` (currently a **stub** — `npm run test:contracts` echoes a TODO and exits 0, not a real assertion yet), `bundle-size` (`npm run test:max-file-size`) → `sit-gate` aggregates all four, `exit 1` on any failure. This is the required check for merging into `release/**`. | | `deploy-dev.yml` | Push → `develop` | `contract-tests` + `bundle-size` gate (`dev-gate`) → `deploy-dev` (`npm run push:dev`) → `tag-sprint` | | `deploy-sit.yml` | `workflow_run` | Only deploys if the upstream SIT Gate workflow concluded `success` | | `deploy-stg.yml` / `deploy-uat.yml` / `deploy-prod.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` only | Manual promotion; `deploy-prod` has **no gate job** — fully manual, relies on the GitHub Environment's required reviewer (see §9) | | `upstream-release-watch.yml` | Weekly cron | Opens a GitHub issue when upstream `pwa-kit`'s release tag differs from the marker in `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md` | | `weekly-agents.yml` | Weekly cron | `quality-sweep` (components/hooks missing a story or test), `contentful-drift-audit` (orphaned `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` files), `changelog-reminder` | **Digital SIT Gate thresholds:** | Signal | Tool | Threshold | |---|---|---| | Playwright P0 | Playwright | 100% pass, all storefront configs, `retries: 0` (flaky tests must be fixed, not retried away) | | Lighthouse CI | LHCI, 3 runs | Performance ≥80, Accessibility ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop blocks | | Contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI (MuleSoft) | Any schema breach blocks — **currently a non-functional stub**, open dependency owned by Zimmermann integration + Accenture delivery lead | | Bundle size | bundlewatch/bundlesize | `main.js` <180kB, `vendor.js` <250–550kB (see §11 discrepancy), `main.css` <50kB | **Known scoping logic worth knowing:** - Change-scoped E2E only narrows to one area (e.g. `checkout`) if *every* e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that single area's allow-list; anything outside falls back to the full suite by design. - Dependency-change detection diffs only `package.json`'s `dependencies` block (not the lockfile) between pushes to decide whether to force `e2e`/`vitest` on. - `Detect Jira story keys` reads PR title/body/branch into an `env:` var (not directly interpolated into a shell command) specifically to avoid shell injection from attacker-controlled PR text. --- ## 4. AI PR Review Tooling **CodeRabbit (`coderabbit.yaml`)** — `profile: assertive`, `request_changes_workflow: true`. - Per-path `path_instructions`: a repo-wide baseline for `overrides/**` (TS-only, SSR window/document guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, i18n, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, a11y, perf, no `console.log`, conventional commits), plus escalated instructions for Tier 1/2 paths (`theme/foundation/**`, the named Tier-1 hooks, `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`, `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`, checkout/PDP/PLP pages, `e2e/features/**`). - Tools enabled: `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `ast-grep` (→ `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), `osvScanner` (OSV.dev dependency vuln scan), `reactDoctor`, `semgrep` (→ `semgrep.yml`). - `pre_merge_checks`: `title`/`description` = **error** mode (conventional-commit format), `issue_assessment` = warning (Jira Forge app not yet installed), custom **`Docstring convention compliance`** check = **error** mode (JSDoc required on shared components/exported hooks/non-obvious utils). - `path_filters` excludes derived config files from review entirely (`.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, `package-lock.json`). **`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`** (mechanically enforces the a11y rules in `.claude/rules/components.md`): - `img-missing-alt.yml` — `` without `alt` - `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — `IconButton*` without `aria-label` - `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — `div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader` with `onClick` but no `role` - `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared matcher used by the three rules above **`semgrep.yml`** (2 rules): - `payment-credential-logged` (ERROR, taint mode) — sources match `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`; sinks are `console.$METHOD(...)` / `Sentry.$METHOD(...)` - `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` (ERROR) — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $X}}` unless `$X` is wrapped in `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)` Both files are Tier 1 — weakening a rule here removes a check with no signal in `coderabbit.yaml` itself, which is why they're locked down alongside it. --- ## 5. Git Hooks (Husky v9) Wired via `.husky/pre-commit` / `.husky/commit-msg` (thin wrappers delegating to `scripts/hooks/`), auto-installed by the `"prepare": "husky"` script on `npm install`. Manual fallback documented in `scripts/hooks/README.md`. **`pre-commit`** (blocking, `exit 1`, unless noted): 1. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` when staged files touch `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`; auto-stages the result. 2. Regenerates `.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` via `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or skill file is staged; **non-blocking** warning if a skill changed and `.claude/skills/README.md`/the mirrored Confluence page wasn't also updated. 3. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen — regenerates `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx`; **blocks** on codegen failure. 4. **Derived-config guard** — blocks any modified `.cursor/rules/*`, `.vscode/instructions/*`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` whose `synced-from:` source file isn't staged in the same commit (prevents drift between AI tool configs). 5. **`.env.sample` secret guard** — blocks if any `_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET`-suffixed key has a non-empty value, or any value looks like a JWT, 32+ char hex, 40+ char base64, or a known provider-token prefix (`AKIA...`, `ghp_...`, `ghs_...`, `sk-...`, `xox[bpars]-...`). **`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits: `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$`, exempting `Merge`/`Revert`/`fixup!`/`squash!`/`WIP`; blocks with a usage message on mismatch. --- ## 6. Claude Code Session Harness (`.claude/settings.json`) - **`PreToolUse`** on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: branch-lock check (see §1) + runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present. - **`PostToolUse`**: Prettier auto-run on new `Write`s; `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (⚠️ referenced but not found on disk — dangling hook reference, see §11) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` on `Edit|Write`; `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh` on `Write`. - **`Stop`**: `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` — if anything changed this session, returns a `block` decision forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/-.md` suggesting doc updates, rather than editing governance docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard to avoid looping. - **`permissions.allow`** pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so routine reads don't prompt. - Client-side hook scripts in `.claude/hooks/` are all **non-blocking** (`exit 0` always): `tier2Warn.sh` (path-matches Tier 2 groups, prints owner/notify warning), `registryUpdate.sh` (incremental `.claude/registry/` regen), `testFileRemind.sh` (reminds, doesn't block, on missing co-located test file). - **Pre-flight skills** that gate *before* Claude acts: `/scope-check` (classifies every file a proposed prompt would touch by tier, verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, rewrites unsafe prompts), `/audit-tier` (tier/owner/blast-radius lookup for a single file). --- ## 7. TypeScript / Lint / Build Enforcement - **`tsconfig.json`**: `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`; path aliases `~/*` → `./*`, `app/*` → `./overrides/app/*`. - **`.eslintrc.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint`; TS-specific rules (`no-floating-promises`, `no-inferrable-types`, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-misused-promises`, `require-await`) are all set to `warn`, not `error`. **Confirms AGENTS.md's own claim**: no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule is configured — the ~150-line/complexity guidance in `.claude/rules/components.md` is a self-check, not an ESLint-enforced gate, today. - **`babel.config.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/babel/babel-config` + `babel-plugin-module-resolver` for the same aliases — part of the path-alias sync group (see §11). - Path-alias sync group is actually **5 files**, not 4 as AGENTS.md states: `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `jest.config.js` (the last for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only — see §11). --- ## 8. Test Harness | Layer | Config | Key settings | |---|---|---| | Vitest | `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.setup.ts` | `environment: 'jsdom'`, `include: overrides/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `passWithNoTests: true`; no coverage-threshold config | | Storybook | `.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx` | `addon-a11y` enabled; `a11y.test: 'error'` — **a11y violations fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs | | Playwright | `playwright.config.js` | `retries: 2` (CI only, `0` for the `p0` project), `workers: 1`; projects: `p0` (SIT gate), `chromium`/`mobile-chrome`, `a11y-mobile`/`a11y-desktop`, `extra-features-*` | | BrowserStack | `.browserstack.yml` | `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope locked — a wider scope means CI cost explosion); Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge across macOS Sonoma + Windows 11; `testObservability: true` synced to Zephyr | | Lighthouse | `lighthouserc.js` | 3 runs; `performance ≥0.80`, `accessibility ≥0.90`, `best-practices ≥0.90`, all error-level | All five config surfaces are Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md`) — a change here breaks every contributor's harness, so they route to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. --- ## 9. Environment, Secrets & Deployment Gates - **`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** (`npm run env`): `init` scaffolds env files from GitHub Environments; `validate [--live]` cross-checks scope placement and can make live read-only Contentful/SLAS calls; **`push ` is gated to tier-1-approvers only** via a live `gh api` identity + team-membership check; `scope:personal` keys are excluded from any centralized push/pull. - **`.env.sample`** scope tagging (`# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto`, own comment line, never trailing) exists specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard. - **GitHub Environments** (per Confluence 304840708 — Environment Topology & Promotion Path): `staging` (no reviewer), `sit`/`pre-prod` (Zimmermann environment owner reviewer), `uat` (Zimmermann stakeholder reviewer), `production` (release-manager manual approval reviewer). SIT secrets are explicitly not accessible to the `production` workflow. - **Promotion path gates**: DEV requires the Digital SIT Gate; STAGE requires Digital SIT Gate green **and** manual NewStore OMS SIT sign-off; UAT requires per-region business stakeholder sign-off; PROD requires release-manager approval **plus** an AU canary (<0.5% error rate over 2h) before wider rollout. - **SIT-specific rules** (Confluence 285540356): manual SIT deploys must use `sit/*` or `hotfix/*`; never push to SIT without Digital Dev green; never enable Einstein/Global-e/Narvar on SIT; SIT is never a hotfix path to PROD (`hotfix/* → main → PROD` only); a broken SIT does not block the Digital release train. --- ## 10. Contentful Sync Safety - **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`** is confirmed additive-only in the actual code: field merging explicitly preserves any existing field not in the local definition (`ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]`) — it can never delete a field from a live content type. - Approval-gated npm scripts (Confluence 318472193): `setup:contentful` and `promote:alias` require a **Tier 1 approver**; `config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver-only, read-only view open to any dev; `sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer. - `detectDrift` runs automatically before migrations apply (bypassable with `--force`) and doubles as a CI-usable gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift). - Contentful environment roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get entry/asset CRUD there but can't touch content types. --- ## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence) Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: *"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."*): | Stage | What happens | Gate | |---|---|---| | 1. Story Intake | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk) | | 2. AC Authoring with Claude | Claude drafts acceptance criteria | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved" | | 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr | | 4. Playwright Spec Authoring | Developer fills in real selectors, confirms local pass | Manual step, no formal gate | | 5. BrowserStack Execution | 7 storefronts × 4 browsers, results auto-sync to Zephyr | Runs on PR to `release/**` | | 6. Defect Triage & Fix Branch | Agent classifies failures by tier, acts within tier limits | **Human Gate 3** — no PR is ever merged without human code review | **AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent guardrails** (Confluence 277708843, most detailed automated-agent doc found): - No auto-merge, ever — branch protection on `develop`/`release/**` can't be bypassed by any workflow or bot. - Tier 1 hard stop is enforced **deterministically** by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup) — never delegated to the LLM's judgment. - Tier 2 auto-fix is permitted, but the PR carries a `tier-2-change` label and a CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer. - Credentials are never placed in LLM prompt context. - Agent PRs carry an `agent-raised` label and a `fix/agent-` branch prefix; CodeRabbit reviews them identically to human PRs. - Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only — no admin/bulk/cross-project). - Runs on **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix) rather than the Anthropic API directly, since the Atlassian MCP integration can't run on a GitHub Actions runner. **Programme-wide Agent Registry constraints** (Confluence 278921217) apply to *every* AI agent in the project, not just this one: Bedrock-only for automated/CI contexts, deterministic Tier-1 stop, no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes, credentials in CI secrets only. A CodeRabbit check also flags any new agent file that isn't matched by a registry update. --- ## 12. Security Boundary Tables (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585) **Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning). reCAPTCHA v3 is the one documented exception — no consent required outside EU/UK, loads only on form interaction. **Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. **SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load). **Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic. --- ## 13. Known Gaps & Drift Worth Flagging These surfaced during the sweep and are not yet resolved — flagging per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule rather than silently ignoring them: - **`test:contracts` is a non-functional stub** — `npm run test:contracts` always exits 0 with a TODO; the "Contract tests" signal in the Digital SIT Gate is not a real assertion yet. Open dependency owned by the Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead. - **`tests/lighthouserc.js` path drift** — `package.json`'s `test:lighthouse` script and both `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS reference a `tests/lighthouserc.js` path that doesn't exist on disk; only the root `lighthouserc.js` exists and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually runs (implicit default resolution, no `--config` flag). Latent, not currently broken, but worth a docs/script cleanup. - **Dangling hook reference** — `.claude/settings.json`'s `PostToolUse` config references `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, which doesn't exist on disk. - **Path-alias sync group is 5 files, not 4** — `.docs/architecture.md` names `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, **and** `jest.config.js`; AGENTS.md's frozenFiles note only lists 4 (omits `jest.config.js`, which serves `pwa-kit-dev` internals only). - **No Renovate/Dependabot bot configured** — despite `coderabbit.yaml` anticipating dependency-bump PR titles (`chore(deps)`), no bot actually opens them; `osvScanner` (via CodeRabbit) is the only automated dependency-vulnerability signal today. - **Confluence vs. repo conflicts** (pre-existing, from a 2026-07-15 audit): Confluence's "Development Standards"/"Component Override Strategy" pages still say to import icons from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` directly (repo says the opposite — always `overrides/app/components/icons`) and to put new components under a `custom/` subfolder (repo convention has no `custom/` layer). "Technical Environment Setup" (304906242) still describes a flat `.env` copy with no mention of the tiered `.env.shared`/`.env.` system. Trust the repo over Confluence where they disagree; these pages need an update. - **Locale count discrepancy** (pre-existing, from the same audit): AGENTS.md/testing.md state "11 active locales" across 8 storefronts; both Confluence locale tables (Contentful Ops page + Product TSD) agree on 9 unique locale codes for the same 8 storefronts. Not yet resolved or raised with the user. --- ## Sources **Repo:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/skills/scope-check`, `.claude/skills/audit-tier`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*`, `semgrep.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc.js`, `babel.config.js`, `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.js`, `.storybook/*`, `.browserstack.yml`, `lighthouserc.js`, `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`, `.docs/memory/*`. **Confluence (space `SFCC`):** 304840733 (Branching Guide), 305561601 (CI/CD Pipeline), 304840754 (SIT Quality Gates), 277544962 + 277577757/277708807/277676053/305528833 (AI-Assisted QA pipeline), 261750785/261881857 (Development Standards / Component Override Strategy), 259358732/259686402/268337165/305430530 (Platform & Tool Access family), 256835585 (Technical Solution Design – PWA), 277708843 (AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent TSD), 305102849 (Human-in-the-Lead AI Development overview), 304840708 (Environment Topology & Promotion Path), 278921217 (Agent Registry), 285540356 (Environment Details — SIT), 318472193 (Contentful CMS Setup & Operations), 264896514 (SFCC Build/Deployment — Headless), 277807105 (QA & Testing index).

content.content: 1 # Zimmermann PWA Kit — Guardrails Overview 2 3 Combines what's codified in the repo (`zimmermann-pwa`) with what's documented on Confluence (space key `SFCC`). 4 5 ## 1. Branch & governance (who can change what) 6 7 - **GitFlow branch rules** (AGENTS.md, [Branching Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)): `feature/*`/`fix/*` from `develop`; `release/**` supervised (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, code fixes only via `fix/release-*` sub-branches); `hotfix/*` from `main`, back-merged to `develop`; `develop`/`main` are human-commit-only and Claude is **physically blocked** from writing to them via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. 8 - **3-tier file protection**: Tier 1 (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` — design tokens, commerce SDK hooks, runtime config, build pipeline, CI/CD, governance files) needs named-owner approval; Tier 2 (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — shared components/hooks, translations, theme components) needs a second reviewer; Tier 3 is plain squad ownership. 9 - **CODEOWNERS** routes every Tier 1/2 path to real GitHub teams (`tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, squad teams); enforced by required code-owner review in branch protection — the actual gate, not Claude's own confirmation prompts. 10 - **Branch protection**: `develop` requires 2 approvals + `unit-tests` status check; `main` requires 2 approvals (both squad leads); `release/**` requires the composite `Digital SIT Gate` check, no admin bypass. 11 - **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`**: `tier1-guard`/`tier2-guard` post warnings/owner-contact maps (non-blocking by design); `branch-target-guard` hard-blocks `feature/*` → `main`; `cross-squad-guard` warns when a PR spans both squads' domains. 12 13 ## 2. Security 14 15 - **Secrets**: never committed — real values in gitignored `.env.`/`.env.shared`, injected as MRT env vars on deploy. `.env.sample` is template-only (names, no values). `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit if a secret-class key (`*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_DSN`, etc.) has a non-empty value or matches a known credential pattern (JWT, AWS `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_`, Slack `xox…`). 16 - **Payment credentials**: never logged/persisted client-side, submitted only in POST bodies, masked after submit (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`) — enforced by the `payment-credential-logged` semgrep rule. 17 - **XSS**: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap a sanitizer call — enforced by the `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` semgrep rule. 18 - **CodeRabbit** (`coderabbit.yaml`) additionally wires in `gitleaks` (secret scanning), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `eslint`, `reactDoctor`, and ast-grep — all as advisory PR-review signal, not a merge gate. 19 - **Env-var security boundary table** ([TSD §4.1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)): every integration credential is classified browser-direct (public) vs MRT-mediated (server-only) vs CI-only — e.g. Contentful Preview/Management tokens, MuleSoft/Booxi/GiveX credentials, and reCAPTCHA secret key never reach the browser bundle. 20 - **Blast-radius containment** (same TSD §12.1): per-upstream SSR connection pools so a flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated ones (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). 21 - **Consent fails closed**: unknown consent state → no third-party script loads at all (Didomi). 22 23 ## 3. Development process 24 25 - Four-step workflow enforced by AGENTS.md: clarify → plan → copy-first (base template files copied to `overrides/` with a marker `console.log` before functional changes) → implement, with an optional local CodeRabbit pass before commit. 26 - TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`, strict mode; no `any` without a comment; DRY/KISS/SOLID; no magic numbers; Australian spelling for Zimmermann code. 27 - **No mocking in production paths** — all data from live Commerce Cloud API. 28 - **Minimal-changes rule**: no upward refactors, no renaming shared hooks/components, no silent scope creep. 29 - Git hooks: `commit-msg` enforces Conventional Commits; `pre-commit` also regenerates derived AI-config files and Contentful `definitions.ts`, and blocks hand-edits to derived config files bypassing their source. 30 31 ## 4. Delivery / CI-CD gates 32 33 - **`qa.yml`** (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): unit tests always run; Storybook interaction + a11y and Playwright are path-scoped to the diff (change-scoped E2E); BrowserStack cross-browser only runs when a Jira key is detected in the PR (develop) or unscoped on `release/**`. 34 - **`digital-sit.yml` / Digital SIT Gate** (required check on `release/**`): Playwright P0 (100% pass, 0 retries — flaky tests must be fixed not retried), Lighthouse CI (Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, no >5pt regression), MuleSoft contract tests (currently a **placeholder**, exits 0 — open dependency pending MuleSoft OpenAPI spec), bundle size (`main.js`<180kB, `vendor.js`<250kB, `main.css`<50kB via bundlewatch). 35 - **Deploy workflows**: `deploy-dev` auto on push to `develop` (gated on contract-tests+bundle-size); `deploy-sit` auto after SIT Gate passes; `deploy-uat`/`deploy-stg`/`deploy-prod` are all manual `workflow_dispatch` only, each behind its own GitHub `environment:` (reviewer protection configured at repo-settings level). 36 - **STAGE promotion** is a manual, non-automated checklist: SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead/squad-lead sign-off. 37 - Weekly automation: `upstream-release-watch.yml` flags new `@salesforce/retail-react-app` releases; `weekly-agents.yml` flags missing tests/stories, Contentful drift, and changelog gaps. 38 39 ## 5. Testing / QA 40 41 - 3 layers, no duplicated coverage: Vitest (logic), Storybook `play` (interaction), Playwright (E2E) — see `.claude/rules/testing.md`. 42 - **Gherkin-first workflow**: `.feature` file → Lead QA sign-off in plain English → Playwright spec generated only after approval. 43 - **Multi-region fixtures** from day one (7 storefronts × 11 locales) — no hardcoded region. 44 - **AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** ([overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962)) with three mandatory human gates: BA approves AC (Gate 1), Tester approves Zephyr cases (Gate 2), Developer reviews any agent-raised fix PR (Gate 3) — the triage agent never touches Tier 1 files, always raises a Jira defect instead. 45 46 ## 6. Accessibility 47 48 - Target WCAG 2.2 AA (2.1 AA floor). Mechanically enforced via `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`: missing ``, missing `IconButton aria-label`, clickable non-interactive elements missing `role`. Plus `vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, Storybook a11y addon, and the Lighthouse A11y ≥90 CI threshold. 49 50 ## 7. Performance 51 52 - LCP ≤2s p75 mobile is the binding constraint. All Didomi-gated third-party scripts must defer/async/post-hydration load (documented exception: Optimizely Web loads pre-render to avoid flicker, US-only). Bundle-size ceilings enforced in CI (above). 53 54 ## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation 55 56 - Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data. 57 58 ## 9. Release & dependency policy 59 60 - Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned. 61 - Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. 62 63 ## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about 64 65 - The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder. 66 - reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff). 67 - GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only. 68 - Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages. 69

Branch & governance (who can change what) - **GitFlow branch rules** (AGENTS.md, [Branching Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)): `feature/*`/`fix/*` from `develop`; `release/**` supervised (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, code fixes only via `fix/release-*` sub-branches); `hotfix/*` from `main`, back-merged to `develop`; `develop`/`main` are human-commit-only and Claude is **physically blocked** from writing to them via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. - **3-tier file protection**: Tier 1 (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` — design tokens, commerce SDK hooks, runtime config, build pipeline, CI/CD, governance files) needs named-owner approval; Tier 2 (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — shared components/hooks, translations, theme components) needs a second reviewer; Tier 3 is plain squad ownership. - **CODEOWNERS** routes every Tier 1/2 path to real GitHub teams (`tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, squad teams); enforced by required code-owner review in branch protection — the actual gate, not Claude's own confirmation prompts. - **Branch protection**: `develop` requires 2 approvals + `unit-tests` status check; `main` requires 2 approvals (both squad leads); `release/**` requires the composite `Digital SIT Gate` check, no admin bypass. - **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`**: `tier1-guard`/`tier2-guard` post warnings/owner-contact maps (non-blocking by design); `branch-target-guard` hard-blocks `feature/*` → `main`; `cross-squad-guard` warns when a PR spans both squads' domains. ## 2. Security - **Secrets**: never committed — real values in gitignored `.env.`/`.env.shared`, injected as MRT env vars on deploy. `.env.sample` is template-only (names, no values). `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit if a secret-class key (`*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_DSN`, etc.) has a non-empty value or matches a known credential pattern (JWT, AWS `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_`, Slack `xox…`). - **Payment credentials**: never logged/persisted client-side, submitted only in POST bodies, masked after submit (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`) — enforced by the `payment-credential-logged` semgrep rule. - **XSS**: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap a sanitizer call — enforced by the `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` semgrep rule. - **CodeRabbit** (`coderabbit.yaml`) additionally wires in `gitleaks` (secret scanning), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `eslint`, `reactDoctor`, and ast-grep — all as advisory PR-review signal, not a merge gate. - **Env-var security boundary table** ([TSD §4.1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)): every integration credential is classified browser-direct (public) vs MRT-mediated (server-only) vs CI-only — e.g. Contentful Preview/Management tokens, MuleSoft/Booxi/GiveX credentials, and reCAPTCHA secret key never reach the browser bundle. - **Blast-radius containment** (same TSD §12.1): per-upstream SSR connection pools so a flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated ones (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). - **Consent fails closed**: unknown consent state → no third-party script loads at all (Didomi). ## 3. Development process - Four-step workflow enforced by AGENTS.md: clarify → plan → copy-first (base template files copied to `overrides/` with a marker `console.log` before functional changes) → implement, with an optional local CodeRabbit pass before commit. - TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`, strict mode; no `any` without a comment; DRY/KISS/SOLID; no magic numbers; Australian spelling for Zimmermann code. - **No mocking in production paths** — all data from live Commerce Cloud API. - **Minimal-changes rule**: no upward refactors, no renaming shared hooks/components, no silent scope creep. - Git hooks: `commit-msg` enforces Conventional Commits; `pre-commit` also regenerates derived AI-config files and Contentful `definitions.ts`, and blocks hand-edits to derived config files bypassing their source. ## 4. Delivery / CI-CD gates - **`qa.yml`** (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): unit tests always run; Storybook interaction + a11y and Playwright are path-scoped to the diff (change-scoped E2E); BrowserStack cross-browser only runs when a Jira key is detected in the PR (develop) or unscoped on `release/**`. - **`digital-sit.yml` / Digital SIT Gate** (required check on `release/**`): Playwright P0 (100% pass, 0 retries — flaky tests must be fixed not retried), Lighthouse CI (Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, no >5pt regression), MuleSoft contract tests (currently a **placeholder**, exits 0 — open dependency pending MuleSoft OpenAPI spec), bundle size (`main.js`<180kB, `vendor.js`<250kB, `main.css`<50kB via bundlewatch). - **Deploy workflows**: `deploy-dev` auto on push to `develop` (gated on contract-tests+bundle-size); `deploy-sit` auto after SIT Gate passes; `deploy-uat`/`deploy-stg`/`deploy-prod` are all manual `workflow_dispatch` only, each behind its own GitHub `environment:` (reviewer protection configured at repo-settings level). - **STAGE promotion** is a manual, non-automated checklist: SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead/squad-lead sign-off. - Weekly automation: `upstream-release-watch.yml` flags new `@salesforce/retail-react-app` releases; `weekly-agents.yml` flags missing tests/stories, Contentful drift, and changelog gaps. ## 5. Testing / QA - 3 layers, no duplicated coverage: Vitest (logic), Storybook `play` (interaction), Playwright (E2E) — see `.claude/rules/testing.md`. - **Gherkin-first workflow**: `.feature` file → Lead QA sign-off in plain English → Playwright spec generated only after approval. - **Multi-region fixtures** from day one (7 storefronts × 11 locales) — no hardcoded region. - **AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** ([overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962)) with three mandatory human gates: BA approves AC (Gate 1), Tester approves Zephyr cases (Gate 2), Developer reviews any agent-raised fix PR (Gate 3) — the triage agent never touches Tier 1 files, always raises a Jira defect instead. ## 6. Accessibility - Target WCAG 2.2 AA (2.1 AA floor). Mechanically enforced via `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`: missing ``, missing `IconButton aria-label`, clickable non-interactive elements missing `role`. Plus `vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, Storybook a11y addon, and the Lighthouse A11y ≥90 CI threshold. ## 7. Performance - LCP ≤2s p75 mobile is the binding constraint. All Didomi-gated third-party scripts must defer/async/post-hydration load (documented exception: Optimizely Web loads pre-render to avoid flicker, US-only). Bundle-size ceilings enforced in CI (above). ## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation - Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data. ## 9. Release & dependency policy - Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned. - Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. ## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about - The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder. - reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff). - GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only. - Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages.
