-## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation
+**Known scoping logic worth knowing:**

+- Change-scoped E2E only narrows to one area (e.g. `checkout`) if *every* e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that single area's allow-list; anything outside falls back to the full suite by design.
+- Dependency-change detection diffs only `package.json`'s `dependencies` block (not the lockfile) between pushes to decide whether to force `e2e`/`vitest` on.
+- `Detect Jira story keys` reads PR title/body/branch into an `env:` var (not directly interpolated into a shell command) specifically to avoid shell injection from attacker-controlled PR text.

-- Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data.
-## 9. Release & dependency policy
+## 4. AI PR Review Tooling
-- Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned.
-- Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`.
+**CodeRabbit (`coderabbit.yaml`)** — `profile: assertive`, `request_changes_workflow: true`.

+- Per-path `path_instructions`: a repo-wide baseline for `overrides/**` (TS-only, SSR window/document guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, i18n, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, a11y, perf, no `console.log`, conventional commits), plus escalated instructions for Tier 1/2 paths (`theme/foundation/**`, the named Tier-1 hooks, `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`, `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`, checkout/PDP/PLP pages, `e2e/features/**`).
+- Tools enabled: `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `ast-grep` (→ `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), `osvScanner` (OSV.dev dependency vuln scan), `reactDoctor`, `semgrep` (→ `semgrep.yml`).

+- `pre_merge_checks`: `title`/`description` = **error** mode (conventional-commit format), `issue_assessment` = warning (Jira Forge app not yet installed), custom **`Docstring convention compliance`** check = **error** mode (JSDoc required on shared components/exported hooks/non-obvious utils).
+- `path_filters` excludes derived config files from review entirely (`.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, `package-lock.json`).
-## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about
+**`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`** (mechanically enforces the a11y rules in `.claude/rules/components.md`):
+- `img-missing-alt.yml` — `` without `alt`
+- `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — `IconButton*` without `aria-label`
+- `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — `div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader` with `onClick` but no `role`
+- `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared matcher used by the three rules above
-- The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder.
-- reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff).

-- GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only.

-- Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages.
+**`semgrep.yml`** (2 rules):
+- `payment-credential-logged` (ERROR, taint mode) — sources match `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`; sinks are `console.$METHOD(...)` / `Sentry.$METHOD(...)`
+- `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` (ERROR) — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $X}}` unless `$X` is wrapped in `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`
+Both files are Tier 1 — weakening a rule here removes a check with no signal in `coderabbit.yaml` itself, which is why they're locked down alongside it.
+## 5. Git Hooks (Husky v9)

+Wired via `.husky/pre-commit` / `.husky/commit-msg` (thin wrappers delegating to `scripts/hooks/`), auto-installed by the `"prepare": "husky"` script on `npm install`. Manual fallback documented in `scripts/hooks/README.md`.
+**`pre-commit`** (blocking, `exit 1`, unless noted):
+1. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` when staged files touch `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`; auto-stages the result.

+2. Regenerates `.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` via `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or skill file is staged; **non-blocking** warning if a skill changed and `.claude/skills/README.md`/the mirrored Confluence page wasn't also updated.
+3. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen — regenerates `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx`; **blocks** on codegen failure.

+4. **Derived-config guard** — blocks any modified `.cursor/rules/*`, `.vscode/instructions/*`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` whose `synced-from:` source file isn't staged in the same commit (prevents drift between AI tool configs).

+5. **`.env.sample` secret guard** — blocks if any `_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET`-suffixed key has a non-empty value, or any value looks like a JWT, 32+ char hex, 40+ char base64, or a known provider-token prefix (`AKIA...`, `ghp_...`, `ghs_...`, `sk-...`, `xox[bpars]-...`).

+**`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits: `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$`, exempting `Merge`/`Revert`/`fixup!`/`squash!`/`WIP`; blocks with a usage message on mismatch.
+## 6. Claude Code Session Harness (`.claude/settings.json`)
+- **`PreToolUse`** on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: branch-lock check (see §1) + runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present.

+- **`PostToolUse`**: Prettier auto-run on new `Write`s; `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (⚠️ referenced but not found on disk — dangling hook reference, see §13) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` on `Edit|Write`; `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh` on `Write`.

+- **`Stop`**: `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` — if anything changed this session, returns a `block` decision forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/<timestamp>-<branch>.md` suggesting doc updates, rather than editing governance docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard to avoid looping.
+- **`permissions.allow`** pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so routine reads don't prompt.

+- Client-side hook scripts in `.claude/hooks/` are all **non-blocking** (`exit 0` always): `tier2Warn.sh` (path-matches Tier 2 groups, prints owner/notify warning), `registryUpdate.sh` (incremental `.claude/registry/` regen), `testFileRemind.sh` (reminds, doesn't block, on missing co-located test file).

+- **Pre-flight skills** that gate *before* Claude acts: `/scope-check` (classifies every file a proposed prompt would touch by tier, verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, rewrites unsafe prompts), `/audit-tier` (tier/owner/blast-radius lookup for a single file).
+## 7. TypeScript / Lint / Build Enforcement
+- **`tsconfig.json`**: `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`; path aliases `~/*` → `./*`, `app/*` → `./overrides/app/*`.

+- **`.eslintrc.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint`; TS-specific rules (`no-floating-promises`, `no-inferrable-types`, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-misused-promises`, `require-await`) are all set to `warn`, not `error`. **Confirms AGENTS.md's own claim**: no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule is configured — the ~150-line/complexity guidance in `.claude/rules/components.md` is a self-check, not an ESLint-enforced gate, today.
+- **`babel.config.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/babel/babel-config` + `babel-plugin-module-resolver` for the same aliases — part of the path-alias sync group (see §13).

+- Path-alias sync group is actually **5 files**, not 4 as AGENTS.md states: `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `jest.config.js` (the last for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only — see §13).
+## 8. Test Harness
+| Layer | Config | Key settings |
+| Vitest | `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.setup.ts` | `environment: 'jsdom'`, `include: overrides/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `passWithNoTests: true`; no coverage-threshold config |
+| Storybook | `.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx` | `addon-a11y` enabled; `a11y.test: 'error'` — **a11y violations fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs |

+| Playwright | `playwright.config.js` | `retries: 2` (CI only, `0` for the `p0` project), `workers: 1`; projects: `p0` (SIT gate), `chromium`/`mobile-chrome`, `a11y-mobile`/`a11y-desktop`, `extra-features-*` |

+| BrowserStack | `.browserstack.yml` | `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope locked — a wider scope means CI cost explosion); Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge across macOS Sonoma + Windows 11; `testObservability: true` synced to Zephyr |
+| Lighthouse | `lighthouserc.js` | 3 runs; `performance ≥0.80`, `accessibility ≥0.90`, `best-practices ≥0.90`, all error-level |
+All five config surfaces are Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md`) — a change here breaks every contributor's harness, so they route to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
+## 9. Environment, Secrets & Deployment Gates

+- **`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** (`npm run env`): `init` scaffolds env files from GitHub Environments; `validate [--live]` cross-checks scope placement and can make live read-only Contentful/SLAS calls; **`push <scope>` is gated to tier-1-approvers only** via a live `gh api` identity + team-membership check; `scope:personal` keys are excluded from any centralized push/pull.

+- **`.env.sample`** scope tagging (`# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto`, own comment line, never trailing) exists specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard.

+- **GitHub Environments** (per Confluence 304840708 — Environment Topology & Promotion Path): `staging` (no reviewer), `sit`/`pre-prod` (Zimmermann environment owner reviewer), `uat` (Zimmermann stakeholder reviewer), `production` (release-manager manual approval reviewer). SIT secrets are explicitly not accessible to the `production` workflow.

+- **Promotion path gates**: DEV requires the Digital SIT Gate; STAGE requires Digital SIT Gate green **and** manual NewStore OMS SIT sign-off; UAT requires per-region business stakeholder sign-off; PROD requires release-manager approval **plus** an AU canary (<0.5% error rate over 2h) before wider rollout.

+- **SIT-specific rules** (Confluence 285540356): manual SIT deploys must use `sit/*` or `hotfix/*`; never push to SIT without Digital Dev green; never enable Einstein/Global-e/Narvar on SIT; SIT is never a hotfix path to PROD (`hotfix/* → main → PROD` only); a broken SIT does not block the Digital release train.

+- **GitHub Environment Variables are plaintext-readable by any repo collaborator** — a deliberate, documented tradeoff for centralization, offset by write access being gated to repo Admin (= tier-1-approvers).
+## 10. Contentful Sync Safety

+- **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`** is confirmed additive-only in the actual code: field merging explicitly preserves any existing field not in the local definition (`ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]`) — it can never delete a field from a live content type.

+- Approval-gated npm scripts (Confluence 318472193): `setup:contentful` and `promote:alias` require a **Tier 1 approver**; `config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver-only, read-only view open to any dev; `sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer.
+- `detectDrift` runs automatically before migrations apply (bypassable with `--force`) and doubles as a CI-usable gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift).

+- Contentful environment roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get entry/asset CRUD there but can't touch content types.
+## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence)

+Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: *"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."*):
+| Stage | What happens | Gate |
+| 1. Story Intake | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk) |
+| 2. AC Authoring with Claude | Claude drafts acceptance criteria | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved" |
+| 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr |
+| 4. Playwright Spec Authoring | Developer fills in real selectors, confirms local pass | Manual step, no formal gate |
+| 5. BrowserStack Execution | 7 storefronts × 4 browsers, results auto-sync to Zephyr | Runs on PR to `release/**` |
+| 6. Defect Triage & Fix Branch | Agent classifies failures by tier, acts within tier limits | **Human Gate 3** — no PR is ever merged without human code review |
+**AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent guardrails** (Confluence 277708843, most detailed automated-agent doc found):
+- No auto-merge, ever — branch protection on `develop`/`release/**` can't be bypassed by any workflow or bot.
+- Tier 1 hard stop is enforced **deterministically** by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup) — never delegated to the LLM's judgment.
+- Tier 2 auto-fix is permitted, but the PR carries a `tier-2-change` label and a CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer.
+- Credentials are never placed in LLM prompt context.
+- Agent PRs carry an `agent-raised` label and a `fix/agent-` branch prefix; CodeRabbit reviews them identically to human PRs.
+- Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only — no admin/bulk/cross-project).
+- Runs on **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix) rather than the Anthropic API directly, since the Atlassian MCP integration can't run on a GitHub Actions runner.

+**Programme-wide Agent Registry constraints** (Confluence 278921217) apply to *every* AI agent in the project, not just this one: Bedrock-only for automated/CI contexts, deterministic Tier-1 stop, no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes, credentials in CI secrets only. A CodeRabbit check also flags any new agent file that isn't matched by a registry update.
+## 12. Security & Privacy Boundaries (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585)

+**Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning; the one documented exception is reCAPTCHA v3, which needs no consent outside EU/UK and loads only on form interaction). Marketing opt-in is unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked), and syncs FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.

+**Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft/Booxi are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. Contentful Management tokens are CI-only, never deployed to MRT.

+**SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load).

+**Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic.

+**Graceful degradation:** each external integration fails independently and has a documented failure mode (TSD §12) — e.g. a Global-e outage must surface an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial/stale data.
+## 13. Known Gaps & Drift Worth Flagging
+These surfaced during the sweep and are not yet resolved — flagging per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule rather than silently ignoring them:

+- **`test:contracts` is a non-functional stub** — `npm run test:contracts` always exits 0 with a TODO; the "Contract tests" signal in the Digital SIT Gate is not a real assertion yet. Open dependency owned by the Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead.

+- **`tests/lighthouserc.js` path drift** — `package.json`'s `test:lighthouse` script and both `frozenFiles.md`/CODEOWNERS reference a `tests/lighthouserc.js` path that doesn't exist on disk; only the root `lighthouserc.js` exists and is what `digital-sit.yml` actually runs (implicit default resolution, no `--config` flag). Latent, not currently broken, but worth a docs/script cleanup.
+- **Dangling hook reference** — `.claude/settings.json`'s `PostToolUse` config references `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, which doesn't exist on disk.

+- **Path-alias sync group is 5 files, not 4** — `.docs/architecture.md` names `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, **and** `jest.config.js`; AGENTS.md's frozenFiles note only lists 4 (omits `jest.config.js`, which serves `pwa-kit-dev` internals only).

+- **No Renovate/Dependabot bot configured** — despite `coderabbit.yaml` anticipating dependency-bump PR titles (`chore(deps)`), no bot actually opens them; `osvScanner` (via CodeRabbit) is the only automated dependency-vulnerability signal today.
+- **reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors** — an accepted tradeoff of the fail-closed consent policy, not a bug.

+- **Confluence vs. repo conflicts** (pre-existing, from a 2026-07-15 audit): Confluence's "Development Standards"/"Component Override Strategy" pages still say to import icons from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` directly (repo says the opposite — always `overrides/app/components/icons`) and to put new components under a `custom/` subfolder (repo convention has no `custom/` layer). "Technical Environment Setup" (304906242) still describes a flat `.env` copy with no mention of the tiered `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` system. Trust the repo over Confluence where they disagree; these pages need an update.

+- **Locale count discrepancy** (pre-existing, from the same audit): AGENTS.md/testing.md state "11 active locales" across 8 storefronts; both Confluence locale tables (Contentful Ops page + Product TSD) agree on 9 unique locale codes for the same 8 storefronts. Not yet resolved or raised with the user.
+## Sources

toolUseResult.originalFile: # Zimmermann PWA Kit — Guardrails Overview Combines what's codified in the repo (`zimmermann-pwa`) with what's documented on Confluence (space key `SFCC`). ## 1. Branch & governance (who can change what) - **GitFlow branch rules** (AGENTS.md, [Branching Guide](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)): `feature/*`/`fix/*` from `develop`; `release/**` supervised (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, code fixes only via `fix/release-*` sub-branches); `hotfix/*` from `main`, back-merged to `develop`; `develop`/`main` are human-commit-only and Claude is **physically blocked** from writing to them via a branch-lock hook in `.claude/settings.json`. - **3-tier file protection**: Tier 1 (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` — design tokens, commerce SDK hooks, runtime config, build pipeline, CI/CD, governance files) needs named-owner approval; Tier 2 (`.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — shared components/hooks, translations, theme components) needs a second reviewer; Tier 3 is plain squad ownership. - **CODEOWNERS** routes every Tier 1/2 path to real GitHub teams (`tier-1-approvers`, `tier-2-approvers`, squad teams); enforced by required code-owner review in branch protection — the actual gate, not Claude's own confirmation prompts. - **Branch protection**: `develop` requires 2 approvals + `unit-tests` status check; `main` requires 2 approvals (both squad leads); `release/**` requires the composite `Digital SIT Gate` check, no admin bypass. - **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`**: `tier1-guard`/`tier2-guard` post warnings/owner-contact maps (non-blocking by design); `branch-target-guard` hard-blocks `feature/*` → `main`; `cross-squad-guard` warns when a PR spans both squads' domains. ## 2. Security - **Secrets**: never committed — real values in gitignored `.env.`/`.env.shared`, injected as MRT env vars on deploy. `.env.sample` is template-only (names, no values). `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit if a secret-class key (`*_TOKEN`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_DSN`, etc.) has a non-empty value or matches a known credential pattern (JWT, AWS `AKIA…`, GitHub `ghp_`, Slack `xox…`). - **Payment credentials**: never logged/persisted client-side, submitted only in POST bodies, masked after submit (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`) — enforced by the `payment-credential-logged` semgrep rule. - **XSS**: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must wrap a sanitizer call — enforced by the `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` semgrep rule. - **CodeRabbit** (`coderabbit.yaml`) additionally wires in `gitleaks` (secret scanning), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `eslint`, `reactDoctor`, and ast-grep — all as advisory PR-review signal, not a merge gate. - **Env-var security boundary table** ([TSD §4.1](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585)): every integration credential is classified browser-direct (public) vs MRT-mediated (server-only) vs CI-only — e.g. Contentful Preview/Management tokens, MuleSoft/Booxi/GiveX credentials, and reCAPTCHA secret key never reach the browser bundle. - **Blast-radius containment** (same TSD §12.1): per-upstream SSR connection pools so a flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated ones (Contentful, SLAS JWKS). - **Consent fails closed**: unknown consent state → no third-party script loads at all (Didomi). ## 3. Development process - Four-step workflow enforced by AGENTS.md: clarify → plan → copy-first (base template files copied to `overrides/` with a marker `console.log` before functional changes) → implement, with an optional local CodeRabbit pass before commit. - TypeScript-only inside `overrides/`, strict mode; no `any` without a comment; DRY/KISS/SOLID; no magic numbers; Australian spelling for Zimmermann code. - **No mocking in production paths** — all data from live Commerce Cloud API. - **Minimal-changes rule**: no upward refactors, no renaming shared hooks/components, no silent scope creep. - Git hooks: `commit-msg` enforces Conventional Commits; `pre-commit` also regenerates derived AI-config files and Contentful `definitions.ts`, and blocks hand-edits to derived config files bypassing their source. ## 4. Delivery / CI-CD gates - **`qa.yml`** (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): unit tests always run; Storybook interaction + a11y and Playwright are path-scoped to the diff (change-scoped E2E); BrowserStack cross-browser only runs when a Jira key is detected in the PR (develop) or unscoped on `release/**`. - **`digital-sit.yml` / Digital SIT Gate** (required check on `release/**`): Playwright P0 (100% pass, 0 retries — flaky tests must be fixed not retried), Lighthouse CI (Perf ≥80, A11y ≥90, Best Practices ≥90, no >5pt regression), MuleSoft contract tests (currently a **placeholder**, exits 0 — open dependency pending MuleSoft OpenAPI spec), bundle size (`main.js`<180kB, `vendor.js`<250kB, `main.css`<50kB via bundlewatch). - **Deploy workflows**: `deploy-dev` auto on push to `develop` (gated on contract-tests+bundle-size); `deploy-sit` auto after SIT Gate passes; `deploy-uat`/`deploy-stg`/`deploy-prod` are all manual `workflow_dispatch` only, each behind its own GitHub `environment:` (reviewer protection configured at repo-settings level). - **STAGE promotion** is a manual, non-automated checklist: SIT Gate green + NewStore SIT complete + Integration Lead/squad-lead sign-off. - Weekly automation: `upstream-release-watch.yml` flags new `@salesforce/retail-react-app` releases; `weekly-agents.yml` flags missing tests/stories, Contentful drift, and changelog gaps. ## 5. Testing / QA - 3 layers, no duplicated coverage: Vitest (logic), Storybook `play` (interaction), Playwright (E2E) — see `.claude/rules/testing.md`. - **Gherkin-first workflow**: `.feature` file → Lead QA sign-off in plain English → Playwright spec generated only after approval. - **Multi-region fixtures** from day one (7 storefronts × 11 locales) — no hardcoded region. - **AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline** ([overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/277544962)) with three mandatory human gates: BA approves AC (Gate 1), Tester approves Zephyr cases (Gate 2), Developer reviews any agent-raised fix PR (Gate 3) — the triage agent never touches Tier 1 files, always raises a Jira defect instead. ## 6. Accessibility - Target WCAG 2.2 AA (2.1 AA floor). Mechanically enforced via `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`: missing ``, missing `IconButton aria-label`, clickable non-interactive elements missing `role`. Plus `vitest-axe`, `axe-playwright`, Storybook a11y addon, and the Lighthouse A11y ≥90 CI threshold. ## 7. Performance - LCP ≤2s p75 mobile is the binding constraint. All Didomi-gated third-party scripts must defer/async/post-hydration load (documented exception: Optimizely Web loads pre-render to avoid flicker, US-only). Bundle-size ceilings enforced in CI (above). ## 8. Consent, privacy & graceful degradation - Didomi gates every third-party script, fails closed on unknown consent. Marketing opt-in unchecked by default except US (pre-checked); syncs FE→SFCC→Omneo→Emarsys, retries silently, never blocks checkout. GDPR (DSAR/erasure) handled by the SFCC cartridge. Each external integration has a documented failure mode (§12 of the TSD) — e.g. Global-e failure surfaces an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial data. ## 9. Release & dependency policy - Supervised editing on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` per `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`; GitFlow back-merges mandatory to keep `develop` aligned. - Upstream `@salesforce/retail-react-app` bumps are opportunistic (security/CVE or a wanted fix), never scheduled, per `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. ## Known gaps / exceptions worth knowing about - The SIT gate's MuleSoft contract-test check is a no-op placeholder. - reCAPTCHA provides no bot protection in EU/UK for consent-declining visitors (accepted tradeoff). - GitHub Environment Variables (used for centralized shared/tier config) are plaintext-readable by collaborators — a deliberate, documented exception to the secrets policy, gated to `tier-1-approvers` only. - Per an earlier Confluence read, the "Development Standards" and "Component Override Strategy" pages still describe a `custom/` sub-folder for new components and a direct-import icon pattern that both contradict current AGENTS.md/repo convention — worth flagging to whoever owns those pages.

48	| `digital-sit.yml` ("SIT Gate")                          | Push/PR → `release/**`             | `playwright-p0`, `lighthouse-ci` (`lhci autorun`), `contract-tests` (currently a **stub** — `npm run test:contracts` echoes a TODO and exits 0, not a real assertion yet), `bundle-size` (`npm run test:max-file-size`) → `sit-gate` aggregates all four, `exit 1` on any failure. This is the required check for merging into `release/**`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
49	| `deploy-dev.yml`                                        | Push → `develop`                   | `contract-tests` + `bundle-size` gate (`dev-gate`) → `deploy-dev` (`npm run push:dev`) → `tag-sprint`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
50	| `deploy-sit.yml`                                        | `workflow_run`                     | Only deploys if the upstream SIT Gate workflow concluded `success`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
51	| `deploy-stg.yml` / `deploy-uat.yml` / `deploy-prod.yml` | `workflow_dispatch` only           | Manual promotion; `deploy-prod` has **no gate job** — fully manual, relies on the GitHub Environment's required reviewer (see §9)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
52	| `upstream-release-watch.yml`                            | Weekly cron                        | Opens a GitHub issue when upstream `pwa-kit`'s release tag differs from the marker in `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
53	| `weekly-agents.yml`                                     | Weekly cron                        | `quality-sweep` (components/hooks missing a story or test), `contentful-drift-audit` (orphaned `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` files), `changelog-reminder`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
54	
55	**Digital SIT Gate thresholds:**
56	
57	| Signal         | Tool                    | Threshold                                                                                                                                 |
58	| -------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
59	| Playwright P0  | Playwright              | 100% pass, all storefront configs, `retries: 0` (flaky tests must be fixed, not retried away)                                             |
60	| Lighthouse CI  | LHCI, 3 runs            | Performance ≥80, Accessibility ≥90, Best Practices ≥90; >5pt drop blocks                                                                  |
61	| Contract tests | Pact/OpenAPI (MuleSoft) | Any schema breach blocks — **currently a non-functional stub**, open dependency owned by Zimmermann integration + Accenture delivery lead |
62	| Bundle size    | bundlewatch/bundlesize  | `main.js` <180kB, `vendor.js` <250–550kB (see §13 discrepancy), `main.css` <50kB                                                          |
63	
64	**Known scoping logic worth knowing:**
65	
66	- Change-scoped E2E only narrows to one area (e.g. `checkout`) if _every_ e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that single area's allow-list; anything outside falls back to the full suite by design.
67	- Dependency-change detection diffs only `package.json`'s `dependencies` block (not the lockfile) between pushes to decide whether to force `e2e`/`vitest` on.
68	- `Detect Jira story keys` reads PR title/body/branch into an `env:` var (not directly interpolated into a shell command) specifically to avoid shell injection from attacker-controlled PR text.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## 4. AI PR Review Tooling
73	
74	**CodeRabbit (`coderabbit.yaml`)** — `profile: assertive`, `request_changes_workflow: true`.
75	
76	- Per-path `path_instructions`: a repo-wide baseline for `overrides/**` (TS-only, SSR window/document guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, i18n, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, a11y, perf, no `console.log`, conventional commits), plus escalated instructions for Tier 1/2 paths (`theme/foundation/**`, the named Tier-1 hooks, `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`, `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`, checkout/PDP/PLP pages, `e2e/features/**`).
77	- Tools enabled: `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `ast-grep` (→ `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), `osvScanner` (OSV.dev dependency vuln scan), `reactDoctor`, `semgrep` (→ `semgrep.yml`).
78	- `pre_merge_checks`: `title`/`description` = **error** mode (conventional-commit format), `issue_assessment` = warning (Jira Forge app not yet installed), custom **`Docstring convention compliance`** check = **error** mode (JSDoc required on shared components/exported hooks/non-obvious utils).
79	- `path_filters` excludes derived config files from review entirely (`.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, `package-lock.json`).
80	
81	**`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`** (mechanically enforces the a11y rules in `.claude/rules/components.md`):
82	
83	- `img-missing-alt.yml` — `<img>` without `alt`
84	- `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — `IconButton*` without `aria-label`
85	- `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — `div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader` with `onClick` but no `role`
86	- `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared matcher used by the three rules above
87	
88	**`semgrep.yml`** (2 rules):
89	
90	- `payment-credential-logged` (ERROR, taint mode) — sources match `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`; sinks are `console.$METHOD(...)` / `Sentry.$METHOD(...)`
91	- `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` (ERROR) — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: $X}}` unless `$X` is wrapped in `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`
92	
93	Both files are Tier 1 — weakening a rule here removes a check with no signal in `coderabbit.yaml` itself, which is why they're locked down alongside it.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 5. Git Hooks (Husky v9)
98	
99	Wired via `.husky/pre-commit` / `.husky/commit-msg` (thin wrappers delegating to `scripts/hooks/`), auto-installed by the `"prepare": "husky"` script on `npm install`. Manual fallback documented in `scripts/hooks/README.md`.
100	
101	**`pre-commit`** (blocking, `exit 1`, unless noted):
102	
103	1. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` when staged files touch `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.tsx`; auto-stages the result.
104	2. Regenerates `.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` via `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or skill file is staged; **non-blocking** warning if a skill changed and `.claude/skills/README.md`/the mirrored Confluence page wasn't also updated.
105	3. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen — regenerates `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx`; **blocks** on codegen failure.
106	4. **Derived-config guard** — blocks any modified `.cursor/rules/*`, `.vscode/instructions/*`, or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` whose `synced-from:` source file isn't staged in the same commit (prevents drift between AI tool configs).
107	5. **`.env.sample` secret guard** — blocks if any `_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET`-suffixed key has a non-empty value, or any value looks like a JWT, 32+ char hex, 40+ char base64, or a known provider-token prefix (`AKIA...`, `ghp_...`, `ghs_...`, `sk-...`, `xox[bpars]-...`).
108	
109	**`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits: `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$`, exempting `Merge`/`Revert`/`fixup!`/`squash!`/`WIP`; blocks with a usage message on mismatch.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 6. Claude Code Session Harness (`.claude/settings.json`)
114	
115	- **`PreToolUse`** on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit`: branch-lock check (see §1) + runs `.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh` if present.
116	- **`PostToolUse`**: Prettier auto-run on new `Write`s; `.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh` (⚠️ referenced but not found on disk — dangling hook reference, see §13) and `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` on `Edit|Write`; `.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh` on `Write`.
117	- **`Stop`**: `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh` — if anything changed this session, returns a `block` decision forcing Claude to write a proposal file to `.docs/agents-proposals/<timestamp>-<branch>.md` suggesting doc updates, rather than editing governance docs directly itself. Has a re-entry guard to avoid looping.
118	- **`permissions.allow`** pre-approves read-only/low-risk Bash (`git branch/status/diff/log/show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`, `npm run lint/test/build`, `gh pr/api/issue`) so routine reads don't prompt.
119	- Client-side hook scripts in `.claude/hooks/` are all **non-blocking** (`exit 0` always): `tier2Warn.sh` (path-matches Tier 2 groups, prints owner/notify warning), `registryUpdate.sh` (incremental `.claude/registry/` regen), `testFileRemind.sh` (reminds, doesn't block, on missing co-located test file).
120	- **Pre-flight skills** that gate _before_ Claude acts: `/scope-check` (classifies every file a proposed prompt would touch by tier, verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED, rewrites unsafe prompts), `/audit-tier` (tier/owner/blast-radius lookup for a single file).
121	
122	---
123	
124	## 7. TypeScript / Lint / Build Enforcement
125	
126	- **`tsconfig.json`**: `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, `skipLibCheck: true`; path aliases `~/*` → `./*`, `app/*` → `./overrides/app/*`.
127	- **`.eslintrc.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/eslint`; TS-specific rules (`no-floating-promises`, `no-inferrable-types`, `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-misused-promises`, `require-await`) are all set to `warn`, not `error`. **Confirms AGENTS.md's own claim**: no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule is configured — the ~150-line/complexity guidance in `.claude/rules/components.md` is a self-check, not an ESLint-enforced gate, today.
128	- **`babel.config.js`**: extends `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/babel/babel-config` + `babel-plugin-module-resolver` for the same aliases — part of the path-alias sync group (see §13).
129	- Path-alias sync group is actually **5 files**, not 4 as AGENTS.md states: `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, `.storybook/main.js`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `jest.config.js` (the last for `pwa-kit-dev` internals only — see §13).
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 8. Test Harness
134	
135	| Layer        | Config                                 | Key settings                                                                                                                                                                                     |
136	| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
137	| Vitest       | `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.setup.ts` | `environment: 'jsdom'`, `include: overrides/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `passWithNoTests: true`; no coverage-threshold config                                                                           |
138	| Storybook    | `.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx`   | `addon-a11y` enabled; `a11y.test: 'error'` — **a11y violations fail** `test-storybook --ci` runs                                                                                                 |
139	| Playwright   | `playwright.config.js`                 | `retries: 2` (CI only, `0` for the `p0` project), `workers: 1`; projects: `p0` (SIT gate), `chromium`/`mobile-chrome`, `a11y-mobile`/`a11y-desktop`, `extra-features-*`                          |
140	| BrowserStack | `.browserstack.yml`                    | `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` only (scope locked — a wider scope means CI cost explosion); Chrome/Safari/Firefox/Edge across macOS Sonoma + Windows 11; `testObservability: true` synced to Zephyr |
141	| Lighthouse   | `lighthouserc.js`                      | 3 runs; `performance ≥0.80`, `accessibility ≥0.90`, `best-practices ≥0.90`, all error-level                                                                                                      |
142	
143	All five config surfaces are Tier 1 (`frozenFiles.md`) — a change here breaks every contributor's harness, so they route to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## 9. Environment, Secrets & Deployment Gates
148	
149	- **`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`** (`npm run env`): `init` scaffolds env files from GitHub Environments; `validate [--live]` cross-checks scope placement and can make live read-only Contentful/SLAS calls; **`push <scope>` is gated to tier-1-approvers only** via a live `gh api` identity + team-membership check; `scope:personal` keys are excluded from any centralized push/pull.
150	- **`.env.sample`** scope tagging (`# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto`, own comment line, never trailing) exists specifically so a blank placeholder doesn't read as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard.
151	- **GitHub Environments** (per Confluence 304840708 — Environment Topology & Promotion Path): `staging` (no reviewer), `sit`/`pre-prod` (Zimmermann environment owner reviewer), `uat` (Zimmermann stakeholder reviewer), `production` (release-manager manual approval reviewer). SIT secrets are explicitly not accessible to the `production` workflow.
152	- **Promotion path gates**: DEV requires the Digital SIT Gate; STAGE requires Digital SIT Gate green **and** manual NewStore OMS SIT sign-off; UAT requires per-region business stakeholder sign-off; PROD requires release-manager approval **plus** an AU canary (<0.5% error rate over 2h) before wider rollout.
153	- **SIT-specific rules** (Confluence 285540356): manual SIT deploys must use `sit/*` or `hotfix/*`; never push to SIT without Digital Dev green; never enable Einstein/Global-e/Narvar on SIT; SIT is never a hotfix path to PROD (`hotfix/* → main → PROD` only); a broken SIT does not block the Digital release train.
154	- **GitHub Environment Variables are plaintext-readable by any repo collaborator** — a deliberate, documented tradeoff for centralization, offset by write access being gated to repo Admin (= tier-1-approvers).
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 10. Contentful Sync Safety
159	
160	- **`scripts/contentful/sync.js`** is confirmed additive-only in the actual code: field merging explicitly preserves any existing field not in the local definition (`ct.fields = [...(ct.fields ?? []).filter(f => !defIds.has(f.id)), ...fields]`) — it can never delete a field from a live content type.
161	- Approval-gated npm scripts (Confluence 318472193): `setup:contentful` and `promote:alias` require a **Tier 1 approver**; `config:contentful` (writes) also Tier 1 approver-only, read-only view open to any dev; `sync:contentful` and `detect:drift` open to any developer.
162	- `detectDrift` runs automatically before migrations apply (bypassable with `--force`) and doubles as a CI-usable gate (`npm run detect:drift` exits non-zero on drift).
163	- Contentful environment roles restrict content-type editing on `sit`/`staging`/`uat`/`master` to the CI service account only — human editors get entry/asset CRUD there but can't touch content types.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence)
168	
169	Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: _"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."_):
170	
171	| Stage                              | What happens                                               | Gate                                                                                                   |
172	| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
173	| 1. Story Intake                    | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template           | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk)                                                                     |
174	| 2. AC Authoring with Claude        | Claude drafts acceptance criteria                          | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved"                               |
175	| 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases                                   | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr |
176	| 4. Playwright Spec Authoring       | Developer fills in real selectors, confirms local pass     | Manual step, no formal gate                                                                            |
177	| 5. BrowserStack Execution          | 7 storefronts × 4 browsers, results auto-sync to Zephyr    | Runs on PR to `release/**`                                                                             |
178	| 6. Defect Triage & Fix Branch      | Agent classifies failures by tier, acts within tier limits | **Human Gate 3** — no PR is ever merged without human code review                                      |
179	
180	**AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent guardrails** (Confluence 277708843, most detailed automated-agent doc found):
181	
182	- No auto-merge, ever — branch protection on `develop`/`release/**` can't be bypassed by any workflow or bot.
183	- Tier 1 hard stop is enforced **deterministically** by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup) — never delegated to the LLM's judgment.
184	- Tier 2 auto-fix is permitted, but the PR carries a `tier-2-change` label and a CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer.
185	- Credentials are never placed in LLM prompt context.
186	- Agent PRs carry an `agent-raised` label and a `fix/agent-` branch prefix; CodeRabbit reviews them identically to human PRs.
187	- Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only — no admin/bulk/cross-project).
188	- Runs on **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix) rather than the Anthropic API directly, since the Atlassian MCP integration can't run on a GitHub Actions runner.
189	
190	**Programme-wide Agent Registry constraints** (Confluence 278921217) apply to _every_ AI agent in the project, not just this one: Bedrock-only for automated/CI contexts, deterministic Tier-1 stop, no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes, credentials in CI secrets only. A CodeRabbit check also flags any new agent file that isn't matched by a registry update.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 12. Security & Privacy Boundaries (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585)
195	
196	**Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning; the one documented exception is reCAPTCHA v3, which needs no consent outside EU/UK and loads only on form interaction). Marketing opt-in is unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked), and syncs FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.
197	
198	**Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft/Booxi are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. Contentful Management tokens are CI-only, never deployed to MRT.
199	
200	**SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load).
201	
202	**Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic.
203	
204	**Graceful degradation:** each external integration fails independently and has a documented failure mode (TSD §12) — e.g. a Global-e outage must surface an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial/stale data.
205	
206	---
207	
208	## Sources
209	
210	**Repo:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/skills/scope-check`, `.claude/skills/audit-tier`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*`, `semgrep.yml`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/hooks/commit-msg`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/contentful/sync.js`, `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc.js`, `babel.config.js`, `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.js`, `.storybook/*`, `.browserstack.yml`, `lighthouserc.js`, `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`, `.docs/memory/*`.
211	
212	**Confluence (space `SFCC`):** 304840733 (Branching Guide), 305561601 (CI/CD Pipeline), 304840754 (SIT Quality Gates), 277544962 + 277577757/277708807/277676053/305528833 (AI-Assisted QA pipeline), 261750785/261881857 (Development Standards / Component Override Strategy), 259358732/259686402/268337165/305430530 (Platform & Tool Access family), 256835585 (Technical Solution Design – PWA), 277708843 (AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent TSD), 305102849 (Human-in-the-Lead AI Development overview), 304840708 (Environment Topology & Promotion Path), 278921217 (Agent Registry), 285540356 (Environment Details — SIT), 318472193 (Contentful CMS Setup & Operations), 264896514 (SFCC Build/Deployment — Headless), 277807105 (QA & Testing index).

# Zimmermann PWA Kit — Software Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails

_Compiled from a full sweep of the `zimmermann-pwa` repo and the Confluence `SFCC` space, 2026-07-16._
_Scope: mechanisms that automatically enforce quality, security, or process — not general conventions that rely on a human/Claude reading a doc._

---

## 1. Branch & Merge Guardrails

| Branch                    | From         | Merges to                                      | Required approvals                                | Notes                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`, `fix/*`      | `develop`    | `develop`                                      | **1** (unit-tests required check)                 | Primary working branches                                                            |
| `release/**`              | `develop`    | `main` + `develop`                             | Required check = **Digital SIT Gate** (composite) | Created by squad leads/CI from a tagged `develop` state, not by developers directly |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | `release/**` | `release/**`, then forward-merged to `develop` | Treated like `feature/*`                          | Only path for code-logic fixes on a release                                         |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`       | `main` + `develop`                             | **2** (both squad leads)                          | Urgent prod fixes only, must back-merge to `develop`                                |
| `develop`                 | —            | —                                              | **2** (one owning squad + one cross-squad)        | Human commits only; required check `unit-tests`, no bypass, must be up to date      |
| `main`                    | —            | —                                              | **2** (both squad leads)                          | Human commits only; same no-bypass rules                                            |

- **Mechanical branch lock (not just documented):** `.claude/settings.json` has a `PreToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit|NotebookEdit` that runs `git branch --show-current` and hard-blocks (`exit 1`) any file write if the branch is `develop` or `main`. This is the actual enforcement of AGENTS.md Hard Rule #1 for Claude Code sessions — GitHub branch protection is the enforcement for everyone/everything else.
- **`branch-target-guard`** (`protected-file-guard.yml`) hard-blocks (`exit 1`) a PR from a `feature/*` head branch targeting `main` directly.
- Release tagging: `scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version}` run from `main` post-merge creates `v{version}` + `release/digital/v{version}` tags; `sprint/{N}/{date}` tags are created automatically by CI (`deploy-dev.yml`'s `tag-sprint` job) when `scripts/sprint.txt` changes.
- Direct commits to a `release/**` branch are restricted to no-logic changes (copy fixes, version bumps, flag toggles) and require explicit squad-lead approval (Confluence: Branching Guide, page 304840733).

---

## 2. File Protection Tiers

Four-tier system, cross-checked across `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, and `protected-file-guard.yml` — all three enforcement surfaces agree.

| Tier                         | Examples                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Enforcement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

## 11. AI-Assisted QA — Six-Stage Pipeline (Confluence)

Three explicit **human gates** in an otherwise Claude/agent-assisted pipeline (per 277807105: _"No AC is approved without BA sign-off. No test case is created without Tester review. No PR is merged without human code review."_):

| Stage                              | What happens                                               | Gate                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1. Story Intake                    | BA structures the Jira story to a fixed template           | none (garbage-in/garbage-out risk)                                                                     |
| 2. AC Authoring with Claude        | Claude drafts acceptance criteria                          | **Human Gate 1** — BA reviews every line, sets Jira status "AC Approved"                               |
| 3. Zephyr Test Case Creation (MCP) | Claude drafts test cases                                   | **Human Gate 2** — Tester reviews and marks "Ready for Execution" before anything is created in Zephyr |
| 4. Playwright Spec Authoring       | Developer fills in real selectors, confirms local pass     | Manual step, no formal gate                                                                            |
| 5. BrowserStack Execution          | 7 storefronts × 4 browsers, results auto-sync to Zephyr    | Runs on PR to `release/**`                                                                             |
| 6. Defect Triage & Fix Branch      | Agent classifies failures by tier, acts within tier limits | **Human Gate 3** — no PR is ever merged without human code review                                      |

**AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent guardrails** (Confluence 277708843, most detailed automated-agent doc found):

- No auto-merge, ever — branch protection on `develop`/`release/**` can't be bypassed by any workflow or bot.
- Tier 1 hard stop is enforced **deterministically** by `classify-tier.js` (a CODEOWNERS lookup) — never delegated to the LLM's judgment.
- Tier 2 auto-fix is permitted, but the PR carries a `tier-2-change` label and a CODEOWNERS-enforced second reviewer.
- Credentials are never placed in LLM prompt context.
- Agent PRs carry an `agent-raised` label and a `fix/agent-` branch prefix; CodeRabbit reviews them identically to human PRs.
- Jira writes go through a scoped service-account token (issue create/link only — no admin/bulk/cross-project).
- Runs on **AWS Bedrock** (Haiku for classification, Sonnet for investigation/fix) rather than the Anthropic API directly, since the Atlassian MCP integration can't run on a GitHub Actions runner.

**Programme-wide Agent Registry constraints** (Confluence 278921217) apply to _every_ AI agent in the project, not just this one: Bedrock-only for automated/CI contexts, deterministic Tier-1 stop, no auto-merge ever, human gate on all code changes, MCP for interactive writes vs REST API for CI writes, credentials in CI secrets only. A CodeRabbit check also flags any new agent file that isn't matched by a registry update.

## 12. Security & Privacy Boundaries (Confluence — Technical Solution Design, 256835585)

**Consent gate (Didomi):** fail-closed — if consent state can't be determined, **no third-party script loads at all**. Everything from GTM/Addingwell, Inside Chat, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Narvar Promise, Measmerize, Vimeo, and Recently Viewed must gate on a Didomi purpose ID (several purpose IDs are still an open item pending provisioning; the one documented exception is reCAPTCHA v3, which needs no consent outside EU/UK and loads only on form interaction). Marketing opt-in is unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked), and syncs FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.

**Credential boundary (by integration):** SLAS client ID is the only browser-direct SFCC credential; Google Maps, Contentful Preview/Management, MuleSoft/Booxi are MRT-mediated only; Adyen/Narvar/Global-e/GTM/Didomi/reCAPTCHA site-key are public-by-design browser-direct values, with their paired secret (API key/HMAC/secret key) always MRT-mediated. Contentful Management tokens are CI-only, never deployed to MRT.

**SSR vs CSR boundary:** PDP/PLP/content/home/boutique = full SSR (SEO/LCP-critical). Cart/checkout/My Account/order history/wishlist/address book = SSR shell + CSR data (personalised, behind auth, blocked in `robots.txt`, and SSR-rendering personalised data risks state leaking across requests under load).

**Blast-radius containment:** each upstream origin (SFCC SCAPI/SLAS JWKS, SFCC Payments, MuleSoft, Google Places, Booxi) gets its own SSR `undici` connection pool with an independent concurrency cap, so a slow/flooded integration (e.g. checkout) can't starve unrelated origins. GiveX balance calls are explicitly flagged as carrying payment credentials and must never queue behind other traffic.

**Graceful degradation:** each external integration fails independently and has a documented failure mode (TSD §12) — e.g. a Global-e outage must surface an explicit error rather than silently falling back to SFCC checkout; Omneo reads are load-bearing for My Account and must show explicit retry UI rather than partial/stale data.

# Zimmermann PWA Kit — Guardrails, At a Glance

A simplified, visual companion to [`zimmermann-pwa-guardrails.md`](./zimmermann-pwa-guardrails.md) and
[`zimmermann-pwa-guardrails-source-map.md`](./zimmermann-pwa-guardrails-source-map.md). Instead of one
giant repo tree, each guardrail category below gets its own small, self-contained diagram of just the
files that back it — so you can look at "Git Hooks" or "CI/CD Pipeline" in isolation without wading
through the rest of the repo.

`⚠` marks a file that's referenced somewhere but confirmed **missing** on disk.

---

## §1 Branch & Merge Guardrails

```
.claude/
└── settings.json              ← branch-lock hook: blocks Claude writes on develop/main

.github/workflows/
├── protected-file-guard.yml   ← branch-target-guard: blocks feature/* → main PRs
└── deploy-dev.yml             ← tag-sprint job

scripts/
├── tagRelease.sh               ← creates v{version} + release/digital/v{version} tags
└── sprint.txt              ⚠  ← read by tag-sprint, not yet created on disk

.docs/
└── releaseBranchesRules.md    ← supervised-edit + back-merge rules for release/hotfix branches
```
Approval counts (1 for `feature/*`/`fix/*`, 2 for `develop`/`main`) are a **GitHub Settings → Branches**
setting, not a file — documented in Confluence 304840733.

---

## §2 File Protection Tiers

```
CODEOWNERS                      ← routes Tier 1/2/3 paths to GitHub teams

.claude/rules/
├── frozenFiles.md              ← Tier 1 (frozen) file list
└── protectedFiles.md           ← Tier 2 (protected) file list

.github/workflows/
└── protected-file-guard.yml    ← tier1-guard, tier2-warning, cross-squad-guard jobs
```

---

## §3 CI/CD Pipeline

```
.github/workflows/
├── qa.yml                       ← unit-tests, storybook-test, e2e-localhost, e2e-browserstack
├── digital-sit.yml              ← playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size → sit-gate
├── deploy-dev.yml                ← dev-gate → deploy-dev → tag-sprint
├── deploy-sit.yml                ← workflow_run, gated on SIT Gate success
├── deploy-stg.yml                ← manual, environment-gated
├── deploy-uat.yml                ← manual, environment-gated
├── deploy-prod.yml               ← manual, no gate job at all
├── upstream-release-watch.yml    ← weekly cron, opens a GitHub issue
└── weekly-agents.yml             ← quality-sweep, contentful-drift-audit, changelog-reminder

package.json                     ← bundlesize thresholds (main.js <180kB, vendor.js <550kB)
lighthouserc.js                  ← perf ≥80 / a11y ≥90 / best-practices ≥90 thresholds
.docs/
└── upstreamPolicy.md            ← "bump opportunistically, not on a schedule" policy
```

---

## §4 AI PR Review Tooling

```
coderabbit.yaml                  ← profile, tools, pre_merge_checks, path_filters
semgrep.yml                      ← payment-credential-logged, dangerously-set-inner-html rules

.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/
├── img-missing-alt.yml
├── icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml
├── clickable-non-interactive-element.yml
└── utils/jsx-element.yml        ← shared matcher used by the 3 rules above
```

---

## §5 Git Hooks

```
.husky/
├── pre-commit                   ← delegates to scripts/hooks/pre-commit
└── commit-msg                   ← delegates to scripts/hooks/commit-msg

scripts/
├── hooks/
│   ├── pre-commit               ← 5 stages: registry regen, cursor-rules sync,
│   │                               Contentful codegen, derived-config guard, .env.sample secret guard
│   └── commit-msg               ← conventional-commit regex
└── syncCursorRules.mjs          ← keeps Cursor/Copilot/VSCode config in sync with .claude/

package.json                     ← "prepare": "husky" (auto-installs the hooks above)
```

---

## §6 Claude Code Session Harness

```
.claude/
├── settings.json                ← PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks, permissions.allow
├── hooks/
│   ├── tier2Warn.sh
│   ├── registryUpdate.sh
│   ├── testFileRemind.sh
│   ├── session-reflect.sh
│   └── contentfulDriftWarn.sh ⚠  ← referenced in settings.json, not on disk
└── skills/
    ├── scope-check/              ← pre-flight prompt-safety check (SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED)
    └── audit-tier/                ← single-file tier/owner/blast-radius lookup
```

---

## §7 TypeScript / Lint / Build Enforcement

```
tsconfig.json                    ← strict mode, path aliases
.eslintrc.js                     ← lint rules (mostly "warn", not "error")
babel.config.js                  ← path-alias sync group (1 of 5)
jest.config.js                   ← path-alias sync group (2 of 5, pwa-kit-dev internals only)

.docs/
└── architecture.md              ← path-alias sync group source of truth
```

---

## §8 Test Harness

```
vitest.config.ts                 ← path-alias sync group (3 of 5)
vitest.setup.ts
playwright.config.js             ← E2E projects, retries, workers
.browserstack.yml                ← cross-browser matrix, scope locked to e2e/tests/zimm
lighthouserc.js                  ← shared with §3 (perf/a11y/best-practices thresholds)

.storybook/
├── main.js                      ← addon-a11y registration
└── preview.tsx                  ← a11y.test: 'error' (a11y violations fail CI)
```

---

## §9 Environment, Secrets & Deployment Gates

```
scripts/
└── switchEnv.mjs                ← init/validate/push subcommands, isTier1Approver() gate

.github/workflows/
├── deploy-sit.yml                ← environment-gated
├── deploy-stg.yml                ← environment-gated
├── deploy-uat.yml                ← environment-gated
└── deploy-prod.yml               ← environment-gated, no gate job
```
GitHub Environment reviewer assignments (staging/sit/uat/production) live in
**GitHub Settings → Environments**, not a file — documented in Confluence 304840708 / 285540356.

---

## §10 Contentful Sync Safety

```
scripts/contentful/

(Confluence 318472193) — no matching `isTier1Approver()`-style check exists in this folder,
unlike `switchEnv.mjs` above.

|---|---|---|
| AI-Assisted QA six-stage pipeline + 3 human gates | 277544962 (+4 guides), 277807105 | §11 |

| Consent gate, credential boundary, SSR/CSR boundary, blast-radius containment | 256835585 | §12 |

# Talking Points — Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails
_For: presenting to Accenture's Innovation Lead (Managing Director)_
_Pair with: `zimmermann-pwa-guardrails-tree.md` as the visual leave-behind. ~3 minute spoken walkthrough + Q&A soundbites below._

---

## Opening — set the frame

> "You asked what engineering harnesses and guardrails we actually have in place on this build — not
> what's on a slide, what's running today. So that's what this is. I'm going to walk it through the
> development process itself: how a change gets from a developer's — or an AI agent's — keyboard into
> production, and what stops a mistake from getting there. Everything I'm about to show you is enforced
> automatically, on every single pull request, not a checklist someone has to remember to follow."

---

## The walkthrough

**1. Ownership scales with the risk of the file, not the size of the change.**
> "Every file in this repo sits in a tier. Touch a homepage banner, normal review. Touch a design token,
> a payment hook, or the CI pipeline itself, and GitHub *requires* a named approver from that domain
> before it can merge — not a request, a hard block. That mapping is explicit and versioned, so nobody's
> relying on someone remembering which files are sensitive."

**2. The pipeline is the first reviewer, before a human ever looks at it.**
> "Before a person reviews a line of code, it's already been through unit tests, accessibility checks,
> a performance budget, and cross-browser testing. A release doesn't get promoted unless all of that is
> green. That means our human reviewers spend their time on logic and intent, not catching things a
> machine already catches for free."

**3. The same guardrails apply whether the code was written by a person or by our AI coding agent.**
> "This is the part I think is actually the interesting one for you. We're using Claude Code on this
> build, and we didn't just write it a policy document and hope. The branch protection is *mechanical* —
> there's a hook that physically blocks the agent from writing to a production branch, full stop, before
> GitHub even gets involved. It gets the same tiered file-ownership rules as a human developer. And there's
> a pre-flight check that scores a proposed change safe/risky/blocked *before* the agent starts working,
> based on exactly which files it's about to touch. The guardrail travels with the tool, not just the
> instructions we gave it."

**4. Nothing ships on an AI's say-so alone.**
> "Anywhere in this process where an AI is doing the drafting — code, test cases, acceptance criteria —
> there's a named human decision point immediately after it. A developer still reviews every pull request.
> A tester still approves every test case before it runs. No merge, ever, happens without that."

**5. The boring stuff — secrets, credentials, content — is boring on purpose.**
> "Commits get scanned for anything that looks like a secret before they even leave a laptop. Content
> syncs are additive-only, so a bad push can't delete something live. Third-party scripts don't load until
> a customer has actually consented. None of this is exciting, and that's the point — it's designed to fail
> safely and quietly, not spectacularly."

---

## Closing — the takeaway

> "The headline I want you to leave with: every change on this build — human-written or AI-assisted —
> passes through tiered ownership, automated quality gates, and at least one human sign-off before it
> reaches a customer. This isn't bespoke to Zimmermann. It's a pattern: branch discipline, tiered file
> ownership, a pipeline that gates before a human has to, and guardrails that constrain the AI agent
> mechanically rather than just on paper. That's repeatable on any account where we're running AI-assisted
> delivery."

---

## Q&A soundbites (if pushed on specifics)

- **"What stops the AI from just breaking something in production?"**
  → "It can't write to a production branch — that's enforced by a hook, not a rule it's told to follow.
  And the highest-risk files require a named human approver regardless of who wrote the change."

- **"Is this mature, or held together with tape?"**
  → "It's real and it's running — but we're not going to oversell it. We ran our own audit of it and found
  a couple of gaps ourselves: one CI check is still a placeholder pending a partner's API spec, and one
  approval step is currently enforced by process rather than code. We'd rather tell you that than have you
  find it first — and both are already logged to fix."

- **"Does this slow the team down?"**
  → "It shifts effort, not adds it. Automated checks catch what used to be manual review time; tiered
  ownership means most changes never touch the high-scrutiny path at all."

- **"Could we reuse this on another account?"**
  → "Yes — the pattern (tiered ownership, pipeline-as-first-reviewer, mechanical AI constraints, human
  sign-off gates) isn't Zimmermann-specific. The file names would change; the structure wouldn't."

# Talking Points — Engineering Harnesses & Guardrails
_For: presenting to Accenture's Innovation Lead (Managing Director)_
_Pair with: `zimmermann-pwa-guardrails-tree.md` as the visual leave-behind. ~3 minute spoken walkthrough + Q&A soundbites below._

---

## Opening — set the frame

> "You asked what engineering harnesses and guardrails we have in place on this build, so I want to
> walk you through where things actually stand — this is what we've put together so far, not a finished
> system. I'll focus on the development process itself: how a change moves from a developer's — or an AI
> agent's — hands into production, and what's in place to catch a mistake along the way. Some of this is
> solid, some of it we're still hardening, and I'd rather be upfront about both."

---

## The walkthrough

**1. We've tried to make file ownership explicit rather than relying on people remembering what's sensitive.**
> "Files are grouped into a few tiers based roughly on blast radius — a homepage banner tweak is treated
> differently to a change touching design tokens or the payment flow. The higher-risk tiers need a named
> approver before they can merge. It's not a perfect system, but the intent is to take 'did anyone notice
> this was sensitive' out of a person's memory and put it somewhere versioned."

**2. A fair amount gets checked automatically before a person even looks at it.**
> "Unit tests, accessibility checks, a performance budget, cross-browser testing — these run before a
> human reviews a change. It doesn't replace review, but it means reviewers aren't the only thing standing
> between a typo and production. Worth saying: one of these checks — a contract test against one of our
> integration partners — is still a placeholder today, so I don't want to overstate that one."

**3. We've tried to constrain the AI coding agent the same way we'd constrain a person, not just tell it politely.**
> "We're using Claude Code on parts of this build. Rather than only writing it instructions, there's a
> mechanical block preventing it from writing directly to production branches, and it inherits the same
> tiered file-ownership rules a human developer would. There's also a pre-check that looks at what a
> proposed change would touch before the agent starts. I'll be honest — this is newer territory for all
> of us, and we're still learning where the edges of it are."

**4. A human still has to say yes before anything ships, AI-assisted or not.**
> "Anywhere an AI is drafting something — code, test cases, acceptance criteria — there's a person
> reviewing it right after. A developer reviews every pull request, a tester approves every test case.
> That hasn't changed, and we didn't want it to."

**5. The less glamorous stuff is deliberately unglamorous.**
> "Secret scanning before a commit leaves a laptop, content syncs that only ever add and never delete,
> third-party scripts that wait for consent. None of this is exciting, and it's not meant to be — it's
> there to fail quietly if something goes wrong, rather than not be there at all."

---

## Closing — the takeaway

> "So that's roughly where we are: ownership that's explicit rather than assumed, some automated checks
> ahead of human review, an attempt to constrain the AI agent the same way we'd constrain a person, and a
> human decision point that never gets skipped. It's not complete, and I'd rather tell you what's still
> rough than gloss over it. If parts of this turn out useful beyond this account, that'd be a nice
> outcome, but it's early to claim that — right now it's just what we've built for this one."

---

## Q&A soundbites (if pushed on specifics)

- **"What stops the AI from just breaking something in production?"**
  → "It can't write to a production branch — that's a mechanical block, not just an instruction. The
  higher-risk files also need a named human approver regardless of who wrote the change. I wouldn't call
  it bulletproof, but it's a real constraint, not a policy on paper."

- **"Is this mature, or held together with tape?"**
  → "Somewhere in between, honestly. We ran our own review of it and found a couple of gaps ourselves —
  one CI check is a placeholder pending a partner's API spec, and one approval step is currently enforced
  by process rather than by code. We'd rather surface that ourselves than have it found later."

- **"Does this slow the team down?"**
  → "There's some overhead, but a lot of it replaces manual review time rather than adding to it. I don't
  have hard numbers on the net effect yet."

- **"Could we reuse this on another account?"**
  → "Possibly — the shape of it (explicit ownership, automated checks, a constrained AI agent, a human
  sign-off that doesn't get skipped) isn't tied to anything Zimmermann-specific in principle. But we
  haven't tried transplanting it anywhere else, so I'd treat that as a hope rather than a proven claim."
